review_text: The fried chicken noodles are very delicious. The dry seafood sukiyaki is good. They give a lot and have a spicy taste. The food comes out quickly and is hot. You can park on the side of the road.

author: Natchapon Nomnunthasab
review_text: This might seem like a strange comment, but I really like the macaroni at the Suki crab fried rice restaurant. It's like my mom's homemade macaroni with lots of ketchup. If anyone recommends the macaroni and suki menu to me, it's delicious. I don't really like the crab fried rice, but I'm more indifferent.

author: Apivigorn Longrak
review_text:
Food: Delicious. The tom yum is rich and flavorful, while the sukiyaki is a bit bland. You can request extra dipping sauce.

Parking: The restaurant is on the roadside, but there's no parking. There's plenty of parking across the street, just a short walk away.

Service: Very staffed. Upon arrival, the staff will bring you ice and are always on hand to assist you.

Opening Hours: The restaurant is open in two shifts: 10:00 AM–2:00 PM
4:00 PM–9:00 PM

author: Maysaya Bass
review_text:
This restaurant is another popular choice when it comes to sukiyaki. They don't have a huge menu, focusing on simple, yet delicious a la carte dishes.

I recommend:
- Mixed Dry Suki: The sukiyaki sauce is excellent, stir-fried with a fragrant wok aroma. The toppings are packed with pork, squid, and shrimp, making it a great value.
- Chicken Stir-fried Noodles: Soft, wide noodles stir-fried with a fragrant wok-fried sauce, served with a generous serving of crispy squid.

This restaurant offers a delicious, balanced meal, with portions appropriate for the price.

author: ice bear
review_text:
A fried rice shop specializing in fried rice. I walked past and smelled the aroma. I saw a few customers, so I decided to give it a try.

The crab fried rice was perfectly cooked, with the rice grains separated and fragrant. The shrimp sukiyaki was fresh and crispy, and the squid was bouncy. It was tasty, but a bit too sweet. Overall, it was a good experience.

It's cute, and there's a sink for customers to wash their hands.

The food is reasonably priced, and the service is relatively quick.

author: Venus Saksongmuang
review_text:
This restaurant's crab fried rice is absolutely delicious... The fried rice is dry and not oily, and they have a lot of crab claws. The portion is very good value for the price. The only downside is that the flavor of the fried rice isn't very rich and is a bit bland.
P.S. You have to add your own chili fish sauce and a squeeze of lime for a perfectly balanced flavor.

author: Cher Ong
review_text:
Latest visit : Visited again after half a year. Ordered 3 different dishes to try. This time around, their taste is not as good as i expect. Their signature black pomfret 🐟 is very normal but very expensive.
1st visit : Quite an interesting Thai restaurant. They don't accommodate too many customers so better make reservation before visiting. Service is not very friendly. Ordered some basic dishes but tasted delicious. The keng som is super duper spicy. For the weak heart, better don't test your limit. The price is a bit on the higher side.

author: mystic delusional
review_text: Beautiful settings, good service and good food. Drinks are not crazy sweet. Almost didn't make it there, glad we did. Should try.

author: Ong SV
review_text: Love this tiny little restaurant that serve dishes with nice plating. Food tastes amazing too. Their petai bit spicy for me. Love the crunchy crab meat spring roll too.

author: Shermin
review_text:
We’ve found the most delicious gems on this trip.
Every dish we tried here was bursting with taste. Limited seating but lucky to have a spot at this delicious spot😋

author: Juliana Ong
review_text: WhatsApp them to make a reservation way before my trip as we went on Christmas Day. They were fully booked, for walk in only avail 7pm and after. Very small restaurant so seating is limited but the restaurant is cosy and clean. Ambience is there, food is delicious and staff fine albeit attitude a bit cold. Take note they only accept cash.

author: Berry Yeap
review_text:
Authentic Thai cuisine in a charming setting! Loved the decor—you enter through a narrow path before reaching the restaurant. 😍✨

🛎️ Without a reservation, you might miss out! We walked in around 5:30 PM and were lucky to get a table. One note: the high chairs for kids here don’t have safety straps. 😅 Thankfully, my little one managed fine.

With just two of us, we couldn't order too much. We tried the recommended appetizers: crab meat spring rolls (180/270 THB), braised pork leg with radish (today's special), stir-fried mani leaves (150 THB), and the spicy seafood soup (300 THB). Plus one rice and two drinks, the total came to 1,095 THB. Overall, a great experience! 😌👌

author: oh wei
review_text:
Foods are savoury and salty . Ordered 4 dishes. The clear soup tomyum is too salty, fried pork is ok. The money vegetable with egg is the most delicious. The foods are not as delicious as the other comments mentioned. Wouldn’t recommend for others to come.The food quality  is not worth for the price we paid. You can find better authentic and local Thai food in other places in Hatyai. This is the worst I had so far.

The staff is unfriendly and rude. Can’t wait for long and roll eyes while taking order. lol what a joke. Bad service overall.

Good atmosphere and ambience though , full of decorations.

author: Lim Chin Chuan
review_text:
A big No No for me to come again...

Food is below average for the price paid...No comment on the taste as this is subjective to individual. But they cant even serve the tomyam hot...i mean temperature hot..

The worst was the bad service...Imagine a boss warn you for a 2 years old kids holding their decorative flower, saying that we need to pay if broken.

After order 5 dishes for a table of four, and 5 dishes for another table of five, I told the staff enough for now and too add later if need more..The boss stand at the back ask me to order now in rude tone otherwise will be slow serving later due to many guest.

No more next time...Thank you for the bad experience...

author: Azhar Rashid
review_text: came in earlier for dinner but not allowed to go in though many empty tables (reservation 630pm) two persons ordered appetizer and main course. waiter nor the cashier bother to ask if we were ready for main course once we finished with appetizer. cashier fridgiting for us to leave by 8pm and even told us after that to leave in 10 minutes. cashier didn’t even know what we had ordered and asked waiter to tell him what we had before issuing the bills. time spent 1 hour 30 minutes including waiting time for both appetizer and main course. cashier could have been friendly rather than faking it to be friendly. told us to leave in 10 minutes with reason to accommodate the next guest was so uncalled for as the restaurant published closing time was 8pm. took me a long time to write this review ‘cause i should have understand people in the service industry better. but not for this restaurant. food was good but not great and service has to improve.

author: Daniel L
review_text: Went there at 5.30 pm, and strangely, pretty much everything we wanted to try was sold out despite opening at 5 pm. on a Friday night. Nonetheless, spring rolls with crab meat and pork were good. Claypot pork trotter has a similar taste to Cantonese style Cheong Zheng. Couldn't taste the other signature dishes and might have had a higher rating given the limited food choices they had at that time. It was disappointing despite being conferred a Thai Select award.

author: say.w
review_text:
The decor was beautifully adorned in the timeless Nyonya style, with its intricate details and vibrant touches.
I savored the delicate flavors of white tom yum, a perfect balance of spice, and the stir-fried bitter gourd with shrimp, which offered a delightful contrast of textures. Simply exquisite and unforgettable!👍👍👍

author: SingWei Wong
review_text: Quits an upmarket experience at a Thai restaurant, food are made freshly n delicious. The serving size is quite substantial, so do not over order in the first round.

author: annt
review_text: We at the restaurant about 6.45pm, didn't make any reservation, waited 20mins in a very hot small tiny "courtyard". Decoration & presention of food looks good, Taste of food are really normal. Staffs not friendly.

author: Siwat Phansuwannakee
review_text: Delicious food, great vibes, and fair pricing. A must-visit!  👍👍

author: Lydia Chin
review_text: Amazingly delicious authentic Thai cuisine. Need to make reservations in advanced as they only have 7 tables. We walked-in and were lucky to get a table. Ordered 4 dishes + 1 soup and came to about 1100Baht. Wanted Omelette Crab but out of stock. So we ordered Stinky Beans + Prawns, Fried pork with brown sauce, Young Coconut shoots + prawns, Glass Noodles with eggs and prawns, and Signature White Tom Yum Seafood. Everything was so good. Highly recommended. Will definitely come back again.

author: Sharon Soh
review_text: It was just behind our hotel so was very lucky to have such a high quality restaurant nearby. Boss was friendly and the place has very nice interiors. Above all food was perfect. Do reserve before visiting to avoid disappointment...or finish your meal before 6pm if you can come early. I will be back.

author: Chee Chin Cheng
review_text: Extremely overpriced. Food is just average. Not worth the price.  There are better authentic thai food at other places. The restaurant is quite small . 5 of us ordered 2 Appetizer and 2 main dishes and it cost us 1730 baht. Only the Appetizer set is good and the sauce is very nice and special. The white tom yam was a disappointment. Not recommended to eat at this place.

author: Iced Latte
review_text: I was there with 7 pax (4 elderly, 1 teenager). Food was alright, wasn't extraordinary. Service was extraordinarily rude though. We ordered their 3 in 1 appetiser and ended up with 4 dishes (fish, omelet, stir fry vege and stir fry tofu). We only wanted to go with 3 dishes but the waitress almost had her jaw dropped and did not want to leave our table and demanded that we proceed with the 4th dish. Two waitresses were unhappy, told us we cant add on orders later cause they have tooo many customers and quickly kept the menu. So if you are not a big eater, dont bother dining here. The restaurant should perhaps put up a minimum spend per table :)

author: Supakij Khomvilai
review_text: I stop by to get famous snack, Caramel Almond Stick and Ar Lua from Chalom shop in front of the restaurant. It's really good taste. You have to try it. Not so sweet and good ingredients they choose for the snack. You will love it ! Recommended.

author: mark phea
review_text: only 5 star rating will represent everything, nothing much can say so..

author: Will Tan
review_text: Nice food, fried rice is very flavorful,  wanton noodle also quite good, fish ball tasted like from SGP in a good way. many tourists driving from Malaysia will stop here for breakfast.

author: Debbie Voon
review_text: The food is good. The fried crab thingy is really good. Enjoyed the wantan noodles too. The drinks were a little strong in color but taste is fine.

author: Cher Ong
review_text: A place that specialises in egg noodles 🍜 & various types of meat. The roast duck & roast pork are delicious. The roast pork has a very crispy & fragrant skin. The ratio of the meat is just nice, not too oily. The crab meat roll is quite nice, but a bit greasy. Ordered the 5 piece set for 2 pax, a bit too much. The egg noodle tastes average. Service is very bad. They have plenty of staff, but none of them are attentive. No smile on their faces & rude attitude.

author: Victor Khoo
review_text: Not a bad place for a hearty bowl of egg noodle soup with mixed meats, 2 prawn dumplings and a fish ball. This is the first time I’ve been here. Since I wasn’t sure which roast meat to have, I went for a little bit of each so I can sample and taste each of them. Crispy roast pork, bbq pork and roast duck. It turns out my favorite was the prawn dumplings.

author: Billy Kok
review_text:
Another recommended restaurant to visit for noodles and rice. Good Thai Chinese food. Reasonable prices. Menu with English and wait staff with knowledge of Chinese dialects.

Fish balls, veggies, sui-kau, roasted duck, crab meat balls (not in menu) and must have their 'leong-fun' ice.

author: Alexander Wong
review_text: Modern chinese restaurant serving their signature wanton noodles, crab meat balls and roast pork. The roast pork has a crispy outer layer with melting fats in the middle. Doesn't have that porky smell and taste very delightful. The crab meat ball for me was alright but has a strong crab smell that I'm unaccustomed to. Otherwise the fish ball and wanton noodle clean flavours and bright ambiance is acceptable.

author: K M
review_text:
What's great?
1) Grass jelly. This is more firm, yummy!
2) Crab roll
3) Prawn dumpling
4) Roast meat platter

What to improve?
Nothing. Maybe bundle some discount with adjacent desert shop?

Visit again?
Yes!

author: Mrs Chew
review_text: I had the wanton noodle soup with roast pork. The noodle is nice and the soup is good. I personally recommend the deep fried crab meat roll, it very flavourful coupled with the Thai chilli sauce.

author: Boonwei Koh
review_text:
Overrated food, no chilli sauce for the meat and the orange juice is very stingy portion.
Wanton noodle taste is below average.

author: Vling Chong
review_text:
There are many branch here, this branch is open most early than others.
Recommend by friend is must eat in Hatyai.
It is delicious enough especially their fried crab ball , Thai milk tea is must also.
Love all the food here, fast service and food be reserve with fast and hot .
Will visit here again next time come back travel to Hatyai 😀

author: Kh Ong
review_text: crispy roast pork.. melts in your mouth.. one of the best i have tried in my life.. crab meat  dumplings, beef tripe noodles great. wanton dumplings equally good.. and dont forget to try the dessert french toast.. a must visit place. price also very reasonable

author: Thian Boon Seng
review_text: One of the best place to have a breakfast in hatyai. Clean, air conditions and good services

author: 00Y
review_text: This spot serves arguably the best wanton noodles in town—springy noodles, tender duck, and crispy siew yuk (no greasy mess!). Their Thai tea is divine, and the mango sticky rice next door (Ken Phu Phang) is the perfect finale. Just two caveats: Parking is tricky, and service can be hit-or-miss.

author: Su Sie Yap
review_text: Popular place for local and tourist.  Roasted pork if u like half fat half meat is good as not too salty.  Char siew soft, good.  Duck meat was tender and deep fried crab meat roll was yummy.  Wantan noodles considered good.  They even have the noodles that you can buy to take back to cook.  Don't have vegetable option, only Kai Lan was available during our visit.  Cold milk tea recommended.  Worth eating here as overall service good.

author: Oscar Tan
review_text: Everything here tastes so good! The restaurant is air-conditioned with a nice vibe as they play a lot of early 2000s classics, and the staffs were mostly friendly. Only thing I can nitpick is that the Pandan Toast was kinda expensive as it costs 119฿. Definitely would return the next time.

author: Ervin Lau
review_text: Delicious shrimp wan ton. Love the crabmeat ball, very juicy. Nice place for brunch. Be ready to have some patient here.

author: Andrew Chan (www.roadtrippers.asia)
review_text: Nice comfortable aircond seating, spacious and clean .. food is good, but I wanted roasted duck, and they were out of it. Shrimp wanton is very nice. Portion is quite generous, and the price is fair. My meal was 155b. Their longan drink is nice too.

author: C T
review_text:
I visited the restaurant around 1 pm on a Tuesday and was delighted to find ample seating available. The noodles were wonderfully tender, reminiscent of the authentic Hong Kong style, and the char siew meat was a particular highlight, absolutely delicious!

The Thai milk tea was a delightful accompaniment, offering a great balance of flavors. Moreover, the restaurant’s prompt service was impressive, ensuring a swift dining experience. The comfortable ambiance added to the overall enjoyment of the meal. A highly recommended spot

author: Alice Woo
review_text: We wanted to try some Wanton Noodles and stopped by Nanyuan Noodle Restaurant for lunch. We ordered a few bowls of Egg Noodle with Shrimp Wanton and Roast Pork, Steam Rice with Roast Pork, Steam Rice with Roast Duck (comes with pickled ginger, half hard boiled egg and cucumber slices), Steam Rice with Roast Pork & Bbq Pork and Egg Noodle with Roast Duck, Roast Pork, Bbq Pork, Shrimp Wanton & Fishball. Both the noodles and rice dishes tasted delicious! The noodles were chewy and the meats were cooked to perfection and tasted so flavourful. They also have dimsum but we only ordered the Steamed Taro Buns, which were a bit too sweet for us. Overall, lunch was delicious and satisfying!

author: YEW KEEN LIM
review_text:
A comfortable shop with several food supply, got noodle, got rice, got some simple Dim Sum.

Tea and juice is very good experience here and staff are friendly, shop owner also very well taking care

Food is good taste and meet the Asia style. Price is reasonable and is worth.

The shop is expanding, next time will have more seat. Hehe

restaurant: จำเนียร Jamnien ( Coffee & Dine )
author: C J
review_text:
The tom yum soup was absolutely bursting with flavor—spicy, tangy, and aromatic all at once. You could really taste the lemongrass, lime leaves, and galangal, giving it that signature Thai kick. The broth had just the right balance of heat and sourness, with meatballs and fresh mushrooms soaking up all the goodness. It was comforting, bold, and totally satisfying—each spoonful warmed me up and made me want more!

The iced Americano Thai Tea was appropriately sweet, creamy, and super refreshing—exactly what I needed to cool down after the spicy soup. It had that rich, deep tea flavor with a hint of spice, perfectly balanced by the creamy condensed milk. Served over ice, it was smooth, flavorful, and honestly kind of addictive.

The cafe does not have air conditioning. So maybe a little bit hot. But overall it is a great spot to enjoy local tomyam and thai tea!

restaurant: จำเนียร Jamnien ( Coffee & Dine )
author: Ng Kah Yan
review_text: I cannot recommend this place enough! While the food was delicious, the staff truly made the experience memorable. Our server was so kind and helpful, she purposely walked out from the bar table, crossed over the road to get a tuk-tuk for us after we had our lunch there. It's rare to find service this genuinely warm. We will absolutely be back!

restaurant: จำเนียร Jamnien ( Coffee & Dine )
author: Duangsamorn Songmuang
review_text: Delicious A la carte .slow cooking.service is ok.chill atmosphere .

restaurant: จำเนียร Jamnien ( Coffee & Dine )
author: Siam Srisuwan
review_text: It's a vintage-style cafe where every angle you take a photo is beautiful. The single-dish meals are also delicious.

restaurant: จำเนียร Jamnien ( Coffee & Dine )
author: laksanan klubtublung
review_text: The food is delicious and the portions are reasonable. It's not hard to find the restaurant.

restaurant: จำเนียร Jamnien ( Coffee & Dine )
author: Amie Yg
review_text: The food is delicious and the prices are reasonable. The menu has Thai and English options and there are many choices. I was pleasantly surprised by this restaurant.

restaurant: จำเนียร Jamnien ( Coffee & Dine )
author: PRU SE
review_text:
Restaurant and cafe
Delicious food, a variety of drinks to choose from, coffee, tea, fruit juice, soda
Mid-range to high prices, but the food and ingredients used with the taste are worth the price
The atmosphere of the shop is loft + vintage, sit and eat, sip coffee, chill out. You have to find parking on the side of the road, but it's not difficult because there aren't many cars on this road.

restaurant: จำเนียร Jamnien ( Coffee & Dine )
author: Jutamas S (Umez)
review_text: The shop has a nice atmosphere, the food is very delicious, and the coffee is quite good. However, the tables are a bit small, making it difficult for diners to place their plates.

restaurant: จำเนียร Jamnien ( Coffee & Dine )
author: Rose K
review_text: All the food is delicious. I really like the soft pork curry rice. Today I ate fried rice with rice noodles. It's exactly like the one I used to eat when I was a kid.

restaurant: จำเนียร Jamnien ( Coffee & Dine )
author: Than Pawannanwanitch
review_text:
Hong Kong style pork rice - The best!
Excellent medium roast Americano
10 out of 10

restaurant: จำเนียร Jamnien ( Coffee & Dine )
author: Araya S
review_text: Ordered through Grab. Price and quantity of food are not appropriate for the portion. Picture is not as shown. Disappointed. Ordered pork dumplings with pickled plums. Thought it was a pig spirit. Expensive compared to quantity.

restaurant: จำเนียร Jamnien ( Coffee & Dine )
author: Pizsanupong Sangkaeo
review_text: Delicious food, friendly service, good atmosphere, suitable for social gatherings.

restaurant: จำเนียร Jamnien ( Coffee & Dine )
author: Palanthorn Loomcharoen
review_text: Delicious food, relaxed atmosphere, and live music at night.

restaurant: จำเนียร Jamnien ( Coffee & Dine )
author: B
review_text: The atmosphere reminds me of my grandmother's house. The food is delicious and the coffee tastes good.

restaurant: จำเนียร Jamnien ( Coffee & Dine )
author: จิรภา หลีมานัน
review_text: The Thai tea is delicious. The shop is beautiful and great for taking photos. The price of the drinks is not too high.

restaurant: จำเนียร Jamnien ( Coffee & Dine )
author: เอียด มะนาวหวาน
review_text: The atmosphere is chill, the food is affordable, and the music is great.

restaurant: จำเนียร Jamnien ( Coffee & Dine )
author: iingz TD
review_text: There are a lot of mosquitoes in the evening, so food comes out slowly.

restaurant: จำเนียร Jamnien ( Coffee & Dine )
author: อภินันท์ รุจิระกรกุล
review_text: Sit back and relax, focus on conversation, not snacks. Comfortable, but there's no backrest. Older people should consider it.

restaurant: จำเนียร Jamnien ( Coffee & Dine )
author: MaiAek agri
review_text: Great and chill atmosphere, delicious food, friendly staff and prices.

restaurant: จำเนียร Jamnien ( Coffee & Dine )
author: แอ๊ด อิน
review_text: I like the decoration of the shop, it is nice and chill. The coffee is nice. The staff are very knowledgeable about coffee.

author: Notorious
review_text: A cozy little coffee shop with a warm, classic home interior that serves a lovely cup of coffee along with other beverages and desserts. It’s not just a spot to unwind — you can also browse through books or enjoy some board games while you’re here. The service is friendly, the atmosphere calm and welcoming, and there’s even a resident cat at the back waiting to play with you 🐱

author: S C
review_text: A charming little cafe that serves great coffee and fresh baked items. Love the decor and staff is friendly.  We had their cappuccino,  dirty latte,  cinnamon bun and banana bread , all better than expectations.

author: Winnn
review_text: To be honest, the drinks here aren’t that impressive, even though the barista and coffee machine look really professional... 😮‍💨 But the environment and setup are great for taking nice photos 📸. So if you’re coming mainly for the drinks, you might want to consider another café. But if you’re here for the vibe and photo spots, it’s a good pick... They even stick a paper "Photo Spots" on some of the chair 🤣

author: Nitikorn Kaewchoo
review_text: This place always makes me feel good every time I come by — whether it's the cozy atmosphere, the friendly chats with the staff, or the warm, down-to-earth vibe from the owner. There's a great selection of coffee to match any taste, and the menu has some real standouts, especially the delicious desserts. Everything just feels right here. It's my favorite spot, and it always will be.

author: SE Teoh
review_text:
went this cafe during weekday, lesser crowds and better experience.
If you come here not sure what to order, I’ll definitely tell you is their Dirty coffee!
I’m a non coffee lover but gt impressed by their Dirty coffee!❤️ every time come Hatyai must visit this cafe!

author: James
review_text: Coffee and carrot cake here are so nice. The atmosphere is really cool as well. Loved it.

author: Jia Yin
review_text: Service is not good. The owner got attitude issue. Rude to paying customers for no valid reason. Bought 4 coffees, about to leave and family wanted to use the bathroom, then started nagging us. The experience was not worth the mediocre coffee. she can ask us nicely but she choose the offensive way, we didnt make noise we just sitting there chilling. she owe us a apologies.

author: Poh Zhi Nan
review_text:
Amazing coffee place in Hatyai! Highly recommend the coffee here which was full-bodied and had the right amount of sweetness and bitterness. I ordered the iced caramel macchiato and there was caramel jelly as well which enhanced the texture and flavour. The tiramisu was also really yummy!

A lot of Malaysians and locals come here, and as a Singaporean, I can certify this place is worth a visit for your coffee fix. There’s also a cat in the house which made my morning. The staff are friendly as well! Will be more than happy to come back and try other drinks on the menu!

author: Min Khant Zaw
review_text: Tiramisu tastes pretty good but their coffee is pretty mediocre. Staffs are quite helpful and nice. However, the atmosphere of this cafe is not that great compared to other cafes in town.

author: I
review_text: Visited on a Monday afternoon. My friend had the medium roast iced americano and I had the light roast tiramisu blend iced americano. I loved my coffee, smooth with a rich aroma. The banana cake was also delicious, not too sweet. They also have a big cute orange cat!

author: ItsJaycee Zhuang
review_text:
Good and nice cafe! Selling coffees and some traditional Thai cakes that are affordable as well! Barista is really friendly that she even shared her experiences and her stories on her coffees!

Please come to try the dirty! It would amaze you!

author: Khoo Jolyn
review_text: A quaint little cafe with a homey feeling. Staff is friendly and helpful and can speak English which helps when we place orders. Types of cakes sold changes everyday. On our visit we had Tiramisu. Drinks are special too and prices are very reasonable.

author: Kanana Kaewsomboon
review_text: This cafe is decorated in a retro style. It might not look very appealing from the outside, but the atmosphere inside is cozy, and all the drinks we ordered were excellent—iced latte, dirty coffee, and iced honey lemon coffee. I’m sure I’ll visit again the next time I’m in Hat Yai.

author: edmund goh
review_text:
Little cosy cafe.
Coffee is good and recommended.
We took the Yuzu americano and 'big dirty' latte and we were not disappointed.
The cookie was superb, too.

Price is midrange .

Not many seats are available, esp if you are a big group.

author: Khansa Gian
review_text: I went there because of the good reviews, and the rating speaks for itself. The place has a cool and calming ambience, the playlist was so good I could hear some of my favorites (CAS, Hozier). Loved their mint chocolate, and the coffee was so smooth I would come back for more. The staff and owner were so kind and friendly to their customers, I had a quick chat before I left just to share what I thought about the place. Hope the business is good so they can stay open to spread the goodness.

author: Wai Kit Lim
review_text: Very good atmosphere, the cafe is using old school design theme which is very pleasant to hang out with friends and family. Must give a try to their pastry/cake !

author: Raymond Wu
review_text: Love this quaint coffee place in the midst of Hatyai Town! The coffee is absolutely great. Not only that, the desserts are superb too which we didn’t expect at all! The owner is friendly and has a love to be pampered cat. Definitely will return here whenever I’m back in Hatyai.

author: art noise
review_text: nice coffee.. nice shop.. friendly owner and staff .. nice cat .. everything is nice

author: Keke Nono
review_text: Found this cafe randomly in Hatyai last weekend. The cafe is so cozy and chill. Tried their light roast Tiramisu blend and love it so much!🤍

author: Alice YJ
review_text:
Love the Dirty Coffee ☕️ of this cafe. Rainy day is an added point as it feels extremely calm looking at the raindrop, taking a sip of coffee while listening the music …
Cute cat which I believe belongs to the cafe owner…

author: Bobby Lornimitdee
review_text: A classic gem in Hat Yai! 💎 AR Restaurant serves amazing Chinese cuisine using the freshest ingredients. Must try: Deep-fried Tofu with Crab Sauce.  Other highlights: Crispy Shrimp Rolls (Hae Keun) and tender Stir-fried Squid with Celery. Their Pork Stomach with Sweet Pickled Greens is also a winner!  Only 780 THB for a feast. Big portions, great price, and 10/10 taste

author: Teng Sook Yin
review_text:
Forgot to snap photos of most of the dishes as it was late and we were very hungry. The dishes were served quite quickly. Tomyam was tasty. So was the pork knuckles and sweet and sour petai prawns. All the dishes were decent except for the shrimp roll which was lacked of shrimp taste or texture. The price was reasonable. The restaurant was packed when we arrived.

Update : We patronized this restaurant again on 15 Nov, 2025. And ordered similar dishes. So managed to snap photos of the dishes.

#Hatyai, #Chineserestaurant

author: Glen Yu
review_text:
Variety of Thai Chinese foods:

AR Restaurant in Hat Yai is a must-visit for anyone looking to experience a delicious blend of authentic Thai and Chinese cuisine. The restaurant successfully captures the essence of classic Southeast Asian dining with its charming, old-school ambiance, making you feel right at home. The friendly staff and quick service add to the welcoming atmosphere, even during peak hours.
The variety of dishes on offer is impressive, with a menu that caters to diverse tastes. Their strength lies in their ability to use fresh, high-quality ingredients, which shines through in every bite. While the restaurant may be more celebrated for its Chinese-style dishes, such as the succulent braised goose and the highly-praised pork knuckle, its Thai offerings are equally outstanding.
For a true Thai culinary adventure, don't miss the Tom Yum Talay, which is a perfect symphony of sour, spicy, and sweet flavors. The Kerabu Chicken Feet is another standout, with its delightful texture and flavorful sauce. The extensive menu also includes a variety of other popular dishes like Fried Fish Maw, Steamed Fish with Soy Sauce, and a range of vegetarian options. The prices are very reasonable, especially given the generous portion sizes, making it a great value for both locals and tourists.
While it's worth noting that some reviews mention a focus on Thai-Chinese flavors rather than the fiery heat of traditional Thai cuisine, the food is consistently praised for its quality and deliciousness. AR Restaurant is more than just a place to eat; it's a genuine culinary destination that truly lives up to its reputation for serving some of the best Thai-Chinese food in Hat Yai."

author: Pk C
review_text: A local seafood restaurant. Generally, the food here is acceptable, especially the fried fishhead, which is really enjoyable. It get really crowded during dinner time and a long queue is expected.

author: Cynthia
review_text:
The sweet and sour petai prawns were delicious — the prawns were fresh and naturally sweet!
The tom yum fish soup was on the sour side, and it came with plenty of king oyster mushrooms, which were really tasty.
The minced pork omelette had small chilies in it, so it was quite spicy — but very flavorful.
All three dishes went perfectly with rice!
We were a group of four and the total was 720 THB.
We visited in the afternoon, and the restaurant was a bit warm inside, but overall it’s a great spot for a good local meal.

author: Simple Simon
review_text: One of my favourite Chinese and Thai restaurants in Hatyai. Been here since the old  chef the father who is no longer here now. Must try fried pork leg and shrimps paste fried. Price and portion is reasonable. Now the son is running the show and can speak Chinese and English.

author: KH (Alson)
review_text: Local Thai Chinese food. Order the recommend food from the menu. Overall is good, serving food is quite fast.

author: Robin CHAN
review_text: AR is highly recommended by hotel staff for its variety and food choice.  Typical chinese style cooking with local flavours. Crab meat unfortunately wasn’t fresh.

author: See Empty
review_text:
We arrived at Ar Restaurant around 3:30pm local time, after a long travel to Hatyai. It was just a short walk from our hotel. We were famished, as we hadn't had our lunch yet. Luckily, the restaurant was practically empty when we arrived, so the food was served quickly after we placed our orders.

First up was the medium sized Seafood Tom Yum. The soup was rich and flavourful, and the spiciness and sourness was just nice. The seafood tasted great too. The medium sized portion was just right for the 4 of us.

Then came Stir Fried Asparagus with Prawns, with king oyster mushrooms in it as well. Simple yet tasty.

Up next was Spicy Petai with Squid. Squid were cooked with the petai beans, along with chillies and basil leaves. It was very delicious and makes me want to eat more rice with it.

Last to be served was the Deep Fried Pork Knuckle. The large size of the pork knuckle shocked us a little when it was served. Among all the food we ordered, this was the best dish. The pork knuckle was covered with delicious crackling, which was very easy to eat even for the elders in the group, due to its crispiness. The meat was tender, and I especially enjoyed the tendon of the pork knuckle, the jelly like substance that was both flavour packed and succulent. My gf loved the dish, even though she doesn't normally enjoy eating meat. While it was already great to eat on its own, we also enjoyed the green dipping sauce that came with it, which had a balanced level of spiciness from the chilli and sourness from the lime juice.

For drinks, they offered a choice of bottled drinking water and sugarcane drink in a bottle. We opted for the sugarcane drink, but while it was too sweet for my taste, the sweetness was a great way to balance the spiciness in the food.

Overall, great food, reasonably priced. I would recommend giving this place a try, especially for their pork knuckle.

author: Yuhng Yeap
review_text:
Lovely old and traditional restaurant serving Thai-Chinese fusion cuisine. Its located inside a very well-preserved old heritage building.

We ordered various of their signature dishes and all of them were pretty good, with a few standout dishes. The best dishes were the deep fried pork knuckles and salted fish kailan vege. The pork knuckle is crispy on the outside, and very soft and tender on the inside, the meat literally melts in your mouth. I highly recommend pairing the meat with the sweet soy sauce that comes with it, absolutely delicious! For salted fish kailan lovers, their rendition is very good. The kailan is not too hard, and not bitter at all. Moreover, the salted fish is very fragrant and flavorful. Highly recommend these 2 dishes!

Some other decent dishes include their tomyum, which is super flavourful and spicy, and the thai-style water spinach. Their crab-based dishes are pretty interesting as they use whole crab meats as the ingredients, which includes the cartilage and sometimes crab shells. It's very annoying to pick away the cartilage and randomly bite into a shell while eating the crab fried rice and egg. However, the taste of those dishes are still pretty good.

Dishes we found slightly underwhelming (but still good) are the shrimp rolls and oyster omelette. The shrimp roll tasted pretty bland without much of a shrimp taste. While the oyster omelette is also pretty bland, I very much prefer the Penang style oyster omelette instead unfortunately.

Overall, it's still an incredible restaurant right in the town center and I highly recommend to try it out you love Thai-Chinese fusion food.

author: Neo TH
review_text: My local friend recommended this restaurant, food is delicious, very local style, must come try, need to wait very long when very crowded. All dish is nice can order and try, highly recommended pork knuckle.

author: M C
review_text: A little pricey but food quality is good. Big servings, good for sharing. Plenty of crab meat in fish maw soup and crab tofu. Can get crowded quickly so come earlier. Cash and QR payment only

author: PL Chia
review_text: The fish here was really cheap and affordable. We had steam pompret, oysters and tom yum at such an affordable price!

author: Chong CC
review_text: This is a famous old shop in Hat Yai. Now it seems that many customers are waiting for food! Both Thai hot and sour and Teochew cuisine are very good.

author: Raymond Beh
review_text:
The dishes arrived looks simple, but the taste is quite good. Recommanded to be one of the food stop for anyone visiting hatyai.

Highly recommand to try their fried egg with mince meat, seafood fried rice and braised pork belly.

author: Crayon Lum
review_text:
Located in an happening area, Kim Yong Market. They serve different kinds of Thai food, and it is suitable for a Chinese stomach. Tom yam tastes good but it's a bit salty, the portion of crab meat tofu is quite big, and crab meat is present too. It might take up to 1 hour upon order during peak hours (7-8pm weekends).
The staff and owner are friendly and helpful, they can speak Mandarin.

author: Song Sean Loo
review_text: The food portion was very large although a bit expensive. The food was nice. Most importantly, they served the food at an exceptionally fast speed. There were lots of ants on the side of my table.

author: Kullakaln G.
review_text: Very impressed, each dish has its own unique flavor and texture. The taste is delicate not too strong but just right. Definitely going back to try another menu.

author: Timmy Chan
review_text:
All the food we ordered was really good. Worth the 30 min wait at dinner time.
Pork knuckle was crispy outside n moist inside. Better than many that we had in famous restaurants in Germany.
Fried oyster was very different from those in Malaysia n it's a must try.

author: Andrew Chan (www.roadtrippers.asia)
review_text:
The food is really nice here .. the pork leg was fabulous, and so was the tomyum. The prawn roll is nice, and so was the chicken feet yam. The only item I personally didn't like as much was the crab tofu as my tofu preference is the local tofu rather than the japanese egg tofu.

Service is good, food preparation is fast, and the environment is that of an old kopitiam. This shop, I think, has been around for a good 50 - 80 years. Prices of food are acceptable for food quality and freshness and also location. It was easily walkable from the Lee Garden Plaza..

author: The Guy
review_text:
Last weekend, I had the absolute pleasure of dining at Kaitainam, a Thai restaurant that’s quickly become my new favorite spot. Tucked away in a cozy corner of town, Kaitainam offers an inviting atmosphere with warm lighting, subtle Thai decor, and a soft hum of chatter that makes you feel right at home. From the moment I walked in, the staff greeted me with genuine smiles and a level of hospitality that’s hard to come by these days.

The menu is a delightful journey through Thailand’s culinary landscape, and I started with their papaya salad—som tam—which was a revelation. The balance of spicy, sweet, sour, and salty was spot-on, with fresh green papaya shredded to perfection and a handful of crushed peanuts adding just the right crunch. For my main, I went with the green curry with chicken, and it was nothing short of spectacular. The creamy coconut milk melded beautifully with the fragrant herbs and tender chicken, served alongside a fluffy mound of jasmine rice that soaked up every bit of that rich, aromatic sauce. I couldn’t resist trying their mango sticky rice for dessert, and it was the ultimate finale—sweet, ripe mango paired with sticky rice drizzled in coconut cream that melted in my mouth.

What sets Kaitainam apart is the attention to detail. Every dish felt fresh, vibrant, and made with care, like it was crafted just for me. The service was impeccable—attentive without being overbearing—and the prices were surprisingly reasonable for the quality. Whether you’re a Thai food aficionado or just dipping your toes in, Kaitainam delivers an experience that’s as authentic as it is unforgettable. I’m already counting the days until my next visit!

author: Cher Ong
review_text: Was stunned by the atmosphere. It's huge with a really nice wooden vibe. Service is bad. We were looking at the menu & the crew were standing & waiting without any patience. We were contemplating what to order, but no suggestions were given. It's just 2 of us & we ordered 4 dishes. Staff didn't warn us about the portion. Was shocked when the dishes arrived. It's good for 4 people & above. We wasted a lot of food. Pricing is high, but the portion is big. Food taste average only.

author: Ken Ny
review_text: Order pineapple fries rice, fries shrimp cake, mango salad and hot pot seafood egg. Pineapple fries rice portion is very big. Overall the food is good and atmosphere is super nice. Services for us is average only. The price for the food, a bottle of beer, coconut and plain water cost 1300bath for 6 persons.

author: Sy Tan
review_text: Good environment, good vibes with many spot to take photo. And very good services by the worker. Food variety is good, many choices.  Worth a try, but food taste have room of improvement . Thai tea is good

author: 胡钰婷
review_text:
The experience was very bad.
We just sat down and were asked what we wanted to drink before we were given the menu. We were given one menu for two people, and asked for another menu and waited a moment. As soon as it came, we were asked if we wanted to order food? There was no paper towel on the table, and they said they would bring it in a while, but they didn't bring it in the end. There were only a few waiters, and they were all serving large tables of customers. They just kept urging us to order food. I won't come again.

author: Rohee Lee
review_text: Tomyam and omelette were tasty! The fried fish is soso only. Overall the service is good the waitress patiently explain the dishes in mandarin. Will come back again for other dishes next time ☺️

author: lee sin jean
review_text:
First time dining here , very good for my first impression. Nice food and clean environment. Although we stay at LeeVana hotel.. it's a 8 minute walk to this restaurant. Fresh coconut water it's a must order in menu. There is a traffic control person outside from this restaurant to manage parking convenient. The food is delicious and the price is consider worthy to the portions. There is a little museum beside this restaurant belong to same boss. The boss also come to greet us welcome.
Definitely will come again here .  Highly recommend for family restaurant.😊😊

author: Kung Chien Pin
review_text:
Worth Trying -Kaeng Som and Fried Pork Knuckle

Prices are quite affordable, and the food portions are generous! If you're dining with someone who doesn’t typically eat a lot, it's a good idea to keep that in mind and avoid over-ordering. Every item on the menu is definitely worth trying, though I must admit, I felt a bit overwhelmed by the wonderful variety of dishes available!

It genuinely took me some time to decide on my order from the menu.

The atmosphere was filled with lovely music from a band until 10PM, but unfortunately, the live performance wrapped up just as I stepped into the restaurant.

author: Sheryn Choong
review_text:
Good food. We had 4 items and cost us thb1200. Service a bit slow but that's probably because it's peak time n a lot of customers.  Server very sweet and apologetic,  but one can see they worked very hard,  serving at full speed as fast as they can.
They also hv a lovely band playing live when we were there on Sat.

author: Alice Ang (艾利斯)
review_text:
Good taste🤭
Is VERY Big portion of the pineapple fried rice😅 i think 6pax also dont even can finish 🤭

author: Edwin Ting
review_text: The waitress here is attentive and can converse in Mandarin fluently. You’ll be spoilt for choice when you see the menu, which includes exotic options like ant eggs. By the way this is a non-halal restaurant.

author: Uachit Petchkong
review_text:
Food is huge portion if come only 1-2 ppl.
If 4-5 ppl it will be great portion.
Found many rare or special menu here.
Food taste Hot n Spicy like authentic southern part of thailand style.
Stuff is really nice service mind.
Price is reasonable for food portion.
Recommend to do have seperate small size portion too then we can try more dishes.

author: Dean Sonetirot
review_text: Best southern Thai food I've had in a long time. The 'Gaeng Som Pla' was the best I've ever had in all of Thailand. Amazing food at a very cheap price 👍

author: Ninven Koh
review_text: Crab 🦀blackpepper not recommend & kemsom soup a little bit salted🐟,vegetable pakliang kai 🥬is taste so yummy

author: Richard Choy
review_text: Family like restaurant. Seafood is fresh and delicious. Service is good. The restaurant boss/cook comes out to check with customers any feedback or comments on the the food serve.

author: loo jay
review_text: Food is Good taste,price also acceptable,but the white face waitress is very very bad service ( boss didn’t give salary or what?)

author: ZX Chin
review_text: Really authentic and yummy southern Thai food located at the edge of Hatyai town which makes it easy to find street parking. Food can be quite spicy but I'm sure you can ask them to reduce that. English menu is available, staff have limited English communication but they were happy to serve with a smile. Will be back to visit again soon with my friends.

author: Tan Chiew Ming
review_text: Food is definitely awesome and for local, not those designated for tourists. Should try for food lover!

author: Min Wen Mo
review_text: Skillful fried vegetable, very delicious 👍🏻👍🏻 but the taste of gaeong som might not suit me, more to sour side and very spicy. Fried Shrimp cake is worth for a try.

author: Millie Voon
review_text: The ambience and decorations are lovely. However, the food are just average and way too salty.

author: Ben Werakit
review_text: From the crowded customers since early morning speaks volume about the popularity of this restaurant. Once they give you table ticket, you can go ahead to pick by yourself the variety of homemade dim sum and other dishes so they will steam or cook for you. The taste is sumptuous and the price is reasonable. Just give it a try and see if you like it.

author: Zen Yong
review_text:
Visited Cook Chai Dim Sum during my trip to Hatyai and it was truly one of the highlights when it comes to local breakfast experiences. This spot is very popular, not only among tourists but also locals, which already tells you a lot about its reputation. If you are visiting Hatyai, this place is often mentioned as a must-try breakfast stop, and after dining here, I can see why.

The staff are friendly and attentive, despite the busyness of the restaurant. Even when the place was quite packed, the service still felt smooth and efficient, which is impressive considering the constant flow of customers.

The environment is lively and bustling, and while it can feel a little crowded at times, it is still comfortable enough for dining. In fact, the busy atmosphere adds to the charm of the place, giving you a sense of the local dining culture in Hatyai.

When it comes to food, there are a lot of varieties to choose from. The selection of dim sum is wide, ranging from steamed buns, dumplings, siu mai, har gao, and many other small plates that are fun to try and share. The food taste is decent—nothing overly fancy, but tasty and satisfying, especially for a casual breakfast. The food portion matches the price, so you get good value for what you pay. The pricing is reasonable, which makes it easy to try a little bit of everything without worrying too much about the bill.

What makes this place even more special is that other than dim sum, you can also order bak kut teh. Having a hot clay pot of herbal soup alongside a spread of dim sum gives you a hearty and unique breakfast combination that you don’t often find elsewhere. It’s definitely worth trying if you want to experience something beyond the usual dim sum.

Overall, I would say Cook Chai Dim Sum is an essential stop if you’re in Hatyai. It combines good food, fair prices, and an authentic local experience. The mix of locals and tourists dining together makes the atmosphere unique, and it gives you the feeling that you’re eating where everyone in town comes for breakfast. Definitely worth visiting at least once during your stay.

author: Rangsan Ruamyoo
review_text:
CookChai Dimsum is a lively and authentic dim sum restaurant that captures both the heart and flavor of Southern Thailand’s food culture. From the moment you walk in, the atmosphere feels warm and bustling, with families, friends, and locals enjoying their meals together in a casual setting. The interior is simple yet full of character, decorated with traditional photos, bright signs, and the unmistakable aroma of freshly steamed dim sum.

The highlight here is, of course, the dim sum itself. Steaming bamboo baskets filled with classic selections such as siu mai and har gow arrive hot and flavorful, with generous fillings and a satisfying texture. Beyond dim sum, the restaurant offers impressive hot dishes. The herbal pork soup served in a clay pot is rich, aromatic, and deeply comforting, blending Chinese herbs with tender meat and mushrooms. Another standout is the sizzling hot plate dish packed with minced pork, mushrooms, and chilies, which delivers both spice and bold flavor. Pairing this with the crispy golden egg omelet creates a balance of textures that complements the meal perfectly.

Service is friendly and efficient, even with the busy crowd, and prices are very reasonable for the generous portions. Overall, CookChai Dimsum is not just a place to eat but an experience that celebrates traditional Chinese-Thai flavors. It’s highly recommended for anyone looking for a hearty breakfast or brunch in the area.

author: Jaris B
review_text: After landed at AOT HatYai, we were randomly looking for good local breakfast place. We found and we ordered dim sum, herb soup, fried buns, and Thai tea. The best part of this place is a signature dessert called "Ginkgo and Taro Sticky Rice Cake" (โอนีแปะก๊วย) SO GOOD and the rest was good, no complain.

author: rudy lee
review_text:
It’s breakfast time, we’re hungry, and let’s face it we need to eat. But that doesn’t mean we’ve lost all standards.

Now, we’re not being snobs here… just practical. Dim sum in Thailand? Really? That’s like flying to Italy and ordering sushi. Sure, it exists but should you? It’s not indigenous, it’s not iconic, and it’s definitely not what Thai kitchens wake up thinking about at dawn.

We’re in the land of tom yum and mango sticky rice. So, while dim sum might be available, it’s a no-brainer to stay away. Why settle for lukewarm siew mai pretending to be Cantonese when there’s a steaming bowl of boat noodles waiting to give you a hug?

Some might say we’re being picky. Nah — we’re just making smart choices with our stomachs. After all, breakfast is too important to waste on mediocrity.

author: Min Khant Zaw
review_text:
Not quite located near city centre but it is definitely worth a travel to this restaurant. Old school vibes with delicious hot steaming dimsum at great price!

To order: get a table and paper with that table number. Bring the paper to dimsum counter and choose whichever dimsum that looks good to you. Pass the chosen dimsums together with that paper with your table number. The freshly steamed dimsums will be delivered to you table a few minutes later.

Place is clean and staffs are attentive too.

author: long koek
review_text:
Came to eat many times....but no chance to review bcos once the dimsum served on table, everyone's chopsticks action faster than camera.

Today i managed to capture few photos.
This dim sum shop is very famous among the local Thai and even the Malaysian Chinese.

The lady boss is charming and her daughter is pretty. The guy boss will fried his golden pla tongko.

Recommended on the fish head fried koayteow. Variety of Dimsum to choose.

author: Alice Sok Peng
review_text: Chokdee closed then we try here. First time. Came around 12pm+ on Thursday. No queue. The bah kut teh and dim sum taste ok. Dim sum cost around 25/40 baht for each. Not sure which one is 25 baht or 40 baht. They will give one order list to order. The paper translated in English and it was easy for customer to order their type of bah kut teh and drinks. We ordered small bah kut teh meat only and ripened pu-er in pot. I would recommend to eat the prawn type steam dim sum. Char siew bao so so. Lor mai gai too strong five-spice powder, personally not prefer. Must eat their half boiled egg, the texture like onsen eggs and taste not like cheap eggs. All cost us around 580 baht if I not mistaken.

author: Simple Simon
review_text: So so compare to Chok Dee Dim Sum in Hatyai. No Air con room. Large size Buk Ku Tay is B380. Abit of high price.

author: Kok Hoong Lee
review_text:
6th January 2024 Visit Hatyai after 9 long months. Decided to have breakfast at Cook Chai Dim Sum together with my Thailand friend. The dim sum  isn't too bad but slightly salty for the chicken leg and pork rib. Surprisingly,  the Bak Kut Teh improved a lot compared to my previous visit.

8th March 2023 Once again, I went back to try other varieties and Bak Kut Teh. Overall, all the items that I ordered were acceptable, and the price is reasonable.

5th February 2023 My first visit to this Dim Sum restaurant in Hat Yai. All the items that I ordered were acceptable but not fantastic.  However,  I think the price is very reasonable for the amount of food that I ordered. (7 items, 1 coffee, and 1 pot of Chinese tea for 186 bahts).

author: Andrew Chan (www.roadtrippers.asia)
review_text:
It is one of the top dimsum spots in Hatyai, but for us Malaysians, please do not compare Thai dimsum to Malaysian dimsum as well as their bak kut teh. Comparable to other dimsum spot in Hatyai, this one is pretty good, food is fresh, and choices are plenty. You can select what you want in the bak kut teh right on the spot too.

Service is good and fast and prices are competitive all over town.

author: Emeline Koh
review_text: Considering an interesting place for dim sum but a bit far from the town. The food here is not really fantastic as what social media have video.  Not as nice as Malaysia dim sum because the taste is quite bland.  The BKT is nothing fantasy and not strong. Might be good for those who like more bland food

author: Ng ys
review_text:
Food is good , very fast working when theres so much customer, thats why no need to queue for long . Xiu mai , har gao, lao sha bao is the best !!!

Bk kut teh taste diff from kl, must try

author: Pk C
review_text: A local tim sum restaurant serving bak kut teh too. Their speciality, fish head with fried flat noodle was nothing to shout about. The fish used was seabass but the flesh has some muddy taste in it.

author: adrian_97s
review_text: Recommended by the hotel owner, this dim sum joint is better than those touristy dim sum place. The bkt is good, not as good as those Klang ones but good enough. The dim sum were different than malaysian dim sum but nonetheless good.

author: Prasit Aphiphunya
review_text:
Excellent breakfast in Had Yai
Great selection of Chinese Dim Sum and others specialties dishes.

Restaurant are full of customers.  Great experiences!!!!!!

author: j s
review_text: Very good quality for the price . You walk over to the counter to select your dimsum n hand it over to be steamed. The noodle is also very good. Be sure to get the table outside if you can as the tables indoor are very cramped and the air inside a little stuffy

author: Denise
review_text: Nearby dim sum to our hotel, place is busy with locals and tourists. Good value and dishes were fresh. Thai coffee was also good. We like the ordering process, you pick the dim sum and they steam it on a tower with your table number.

author: Yelloboi Jaysen TJ
review_text: Assorted dim sum in hatyai. At least, no need long queue like cheok dee dim sum. Beautifully craft design mini dimsum. Taste average. Only steamed after ordering.

author: Shernny
review_text:
Local Favourite and It’s my favourite too.
Like their fried noodle and fish , the crunchiness of the noodle..yum.
I can just eat the Bak Kut Teh without rice as it is not to salty and just perfect.
Hatyai You Zha Kuih is a must eat. Plain without dipping sauce is my favourite.
Highly Recommend to visit.

author: Lauren Yoon
review_text:
The food comes out quickly. I think my health will get better after eating hot “bak kut teh”.  My mom said it was her first time eating bakute and it was so delicious.
It was a very good meal for the price
because many dim sum came out at a low price👍🏼👍🏼

author: Joon Wei Teow
review_text:
A popular dim sum spot offering a delightful fusion of Thai and Chinese flavors. The variety of dim sum options is impressive, catering to different tastes with flavorful and well-prepared dishes. The taste is satisfying, making it a great place to enjoy a hearty meal.

However, the dining area is quite packed with tables, making it a bit challenging to move around comfortably. The staff are busy and rushing to serve customers, which adds to the lively but slightly chaotic atmosphere. Despite this, getting a seat isn’t too difficult, and the pricing remains reasonable.

Overall, it’s a must-visit spot when in Hatyai, especially for dim sum lovers looking to experience a unique Thai-Chinese twist.

author: K M
review_text:
What's great?
Came here as Chokdee was closed. A different style of dim sum here. The music is most apt. Fried Gu Cai Kueh is the best.

What's to improve?
Found a dead housefly on one of the lettuce! Skip the salmon, it is overcooked.

Visit again?
Yes, but skip the lettuce.

author: Alice Woo
review_text: Our tour guide K. Mimi, suggested dim sum for breakfast and took us to Ama Dimsum. This restaurant is cozy, spacious and have different sections for indoor seating or with air conditioning. It’s like a ‘buffet style spread’ where you can choose and pick the dishes you like, thus no menu is needed. There is a huge variety of dimsum offered and you can eat to your heart’s content! Some dishes are pre-cooked, baked, fried and ready to be eaten. After you have selected your choices of uncooked dishes, you can hand the tray over to the staff and they will steam and warm up the food for you. We chose some traditional style dishes to try but our teenagers preferred those assorted flavoured fish balls. Overall, food was tasty and prices were reasonable with the portion size given. It’s not as authentic as the Hong Kong style dim sum but still good. This restaurant is a tourist spot for breakfast/ brunch, so expect a large crowd especially on weekends.

author: Seeker Star
review_text: The dim sum taste compared to Malaysia, I still prefer Malaysia. There is no juicy and normal taste. The space is big and will be available for you. The foods to steam but consider fast service.

author: Honzie Khong
review_text: Instead of the better know tourist dim sum place you should venture a little further out to A Ma's This has a 60 years history and the place is very nice and comfy.  Choose your dimsum and it'll be on your table in time for the tea to brew. What's good. The hargow, bitter gourd, phoenix claw Thai style, Chai kueh, are worth the try. But what's surprisingly good is their char siew wanton noodle . Can fight with KL. All in very enjoyable breakfast. Reasonable for 9 pax 1275 Baht.

author: cys edi
review_text: Food is so so and not the truly authentic Hong Kong style and standard. Probably the local interpretation of tim sum. The tim sum are pre prepared or frozen and steam on the spot. Nevertheless, it is a place to enjoy tim sum with the festivity mood as it is crowded and lots of people moving around enjoying the eats. Price is reasonable. Service is friendly and cordial. Overall quite enjoyable social eating.

author: Kenny Chong
review_text:
The variety considered a lot. Staff are quite friendly. Good not so bad. Bak kut Teh is kind of different. Overall can consider to come for breakfast.

This place is easy to find with the signature logo. The staff can converse in Mandarin.

author: CS Chai
review_text: This dim sum restaurant is among the more popular ones in Hatyai. Big sitting area including the non air-cond section at the side. Diners choose the dishes and the waitresses send them to be steamed in the kitchen. Kon loh mee, fish, pork and prawn porridge, bak kut teh and pork leg stew are also available. Free Wifi.  Accept cash only.

author: Bigman
review_text:
Came here to have my Dim sum with my friends - place is aircon and you get to pick your Dim sum and give it to the waiter with your table number
Taste to me is so so only compare the other more popular dim sum outlets
I still prefer the other Dim Sum taste

author: Rui Woon
review_text: This review got a 3 star purely base on food. Dim sum originated from the China and is consider part of Kantonese dish. If you are from China especially Hong Kong Malaysia, Singapore, I'll say give it a pass.

author: Kancy Eng
review_text:
Healthy dim sum. Fresh ingredients. Lack of varieties compared to chok Dee.
A bit bland taste.
Nice aircon environment.

author: sh ewe
review_text: AMA Dimsum has great deco homely atmosphere. Service is excellent with great selection of dim sum.

author: Peewara Chaichart
review_text: Nice place to enjoyed Breakfast. Not very crowded from Tourists tour like other Dimsum place in Hatyai but I can say the quality is great, clean and fast service. Various choices of food from Dimsum, Congee, Fried stuff and Ba-Kut-Teh(Pork stew).

author: Jiunnfa Khoo
review_text:
Congee is the best food available here for me.

Dimsums are just average. Place is cozy with air-conditioning. Worth a stop before going to songkla from hatyai

author: Nicholas Woo
review_text: Super nice dim sum with affordable price. More than 50 variants to choose from!

author: CoMeToPaPa
review_text: In Thailand if its dim sum.. Its not that big of a deal.. But for a try sure give it a shot... Malaysia dim sum is better

author: John lcf
review_text:
Very disappointed with both the food and service. The food portions were shockingly small, especially considering the high prices.

The owner seemed more interested in simply calculating the bill rather than providing an honest and pleasant dining experience.

Overall, I will not recommend "Ama dim sum" There are many other restaurants in hatyai that offer better food, fairer prices, and more honest service...
Sorry for given the poor fedback, but this is really my honest experience..

author: Tan Wei Sheng
review_text:
The foods are below par on the price paid. Limited selections and most of the items in store are pretty dull.

Service wise was a-okay.

Atmosphere is another down point as it's just too crowded. Bus loads of tourists tend to come in which seems to hype up the place but definitely not worth a 4* review.

author: Porntipa Sae-Kee
review_text:
Nice place for quick and yummy breakfast, the food is mainly DimSum: love adding the 'Cik Chow' (Chinese vinegar-black sauce on the table).

Apart from Dimsum, We also tried pork congee, it was a pork ball with egg in the congee, easy to eat and test better adding some pepper powder (personal preference) the portion is on the larger size in comparison with usual Dimsum shop that sell congee.

The wait time is reasonable and the staff could communicate in several languages. The price is reasonable, the shop is clean and good airflow. The parking is not too challenging to find (Note: we go on weekdays)

author: Alice Woo
review_text: This small restaurant serves some delicious Duck Noodles. You can have your noodles dry or with soup and with mixed meats. The noodles were very chewy and the broth tasted delicious and very flavourful. As for the duck meat.. it’s soft, tender and very tasty. They were very generous with the spring onions and crispy fried onions. You can add extra sauces if you like your noodle a bit spicier or more flavourful. We enjoyed eating the noodles very much… so yummy!

author: May L
review_text:
Decent local eats. Comfort food after all the spicy Thai food.
Bitter gourd stuffed with minced meat is so good. We had multiple servings of that dish.  All other dishes are acceptable.

Service a bit slow.

author: Terry Yee
review_text:
This is no 4 star restaurant but I would give 4 star for their duck noodle soup!

The broth is flavourful, the duck meat is just tender nice and adding on the fish sauce and chilli just make my first meal here after reaching so beautiful. ☺️

author: Chong Lip
review_text:
Great backyard Duck Noodle…amazingly nice…😋👏🏻👍🏻👍🏻
No doubt…must try if come Hatyai

author: Charles Chan
review_text: In the vicinity of Golden Crown Grand Hotel in Hadyai (this is a great option to Lee Garden which is often a choice for most Malaysian) are tons of little gem/stalls if you could not sleep and want to avoid crowded and touristy spots. I’m sharing a truly hidden gem called Hadyai Duck Noodles. Open for business only in the evening at 5pm and stay open till 4 or 5am. Local taste but the ingredients of duck parts , duck blood cubes and legs (not the drumsticks)😂😂😂😂😂. The soup is a bit peppery but lightly induced, might have some “msg” and loved the taste overall. Sharing so that other visitors can have another choice in terms of midnight snacks.

author: Bosco Khoo
review_text: There are 2 stalls here, no. 16 and no. 20. This one is right at the corner of the alleyway (No. 20). The lady boss knows Mandarin language. I chose a bowl of duck noodles soup, it tastes good. More locals are seen eating here than at the other stall. Support it.

author: Nicholas Lai
review_text: Try their duck soup noodle, is yummy. You would not get it in Malaysia.

author: WY Lau
review_text: This duck noodles didn’t meet my expectations. The soup is clear soup, a lot of pepper powder added into it. Portion is small but the duck still ok and it is soft. The place is hidden and not easy to find. The surrounding is dark and got mosquito.

author: Mel
review_text: The soup broth for our noodles was rather watered down, good if you’re looking for something light and flavours that are not overpowering. The pork balls are springy and has a good bite! Would go back again for the pork balls.

author: Harry Lee
review_text: Can order in Chinese. My dad say the current proprietress is second generation. Soup is used to be thicker. Still quite nice now.

author: dawn sun
review_text:
Simple yet so delicious! Such a comfort food.
It’s a must have, where locals would go instead of going to the Main Street.

author: Seth L
review_text:
Really great food, had trouble deciding which store to eat since there are two stores selling the same dishes. But after trying this place I definitely think this is much better.

Staff was also extremely friendly. 10/10 would recommend

author: PH Yeap
review_text: More locals came here compared to another shop selling the same thing besides. Lady boss was friendly , noodle best taken as dry version with soup separate

author: Anthony I
review_text: Good duck and chicken soup n noodles nice flavour with ginger and other spices,love the green noodles

author: Arisuありす
review_text:
Yummy duck noodles soup in the midnight..
Siew Mai a bit sweet, not my taste..

author: Yuwalak Uthairangsi
review_text: Chicken thighs is my fav and duck thighs for my mom. Been eating here since I was a kid

author: LEE TONY
review_text:
I had a very satisfying duck noodle soup at Duck Noodle Hatyai. The owner and wait staff were very welcoming and warmly welcomed everyone, making everyone feel right at home. While the restaurant isn't particularly upscale, with seating outdoors, the atmosphere is relaxed and comfortable.

The menu offers a variety of noodle options, all of which were very delicious. The duck broth was savory and the toppings were plentiful—very tasty. The prices were very reasonable for Malaysians, making it a great value.

If you enjoy noodles, especially duck noodle soup, this place is highly recommended. After learning about this place, I'll definitely recommend it to my friends and family who love noodles, and I'll definitely be back!

author: Fah Lunla And Luna
review_text:
Duck leg noodles are good. For those who like a mild ginger soup, the ginger smell is not too strong. This shop is good.
The duck meat is well-made, tender, not tough, no fishy smell. When cut, it falls off the bone. The innards are clean and well-made, no smell.

- Steamed dumplings are very delicious. Dip them with the shop's dipping sauce. There is sweet and sour sauce.
* But the shop doesn't steam them fresh in the microwave, so some parts are a bit hard, but only a little.

author: YAP FLY
review_text:
This is a three-generation duck leg noodle shop!
It's located next to the Grand Hyatt Hotel (a short walk down the street)! With decades of service and its reputation, it quickly fills up after 8:00 PM, mostly with tourists.
The clear duck leg noodle soup has a subtle ginger flavor (Malaysians might find it a bit bland, but compared to other clear broths, it's quite good). The duck leg is perfectly tender and delicious. 👍
The food was a little slow to arrive, though. We waited 20 minutes for our food, even though there were still two or three bowls ahead of us.

author: Eleanor Li
review_text: I couldn't sleep because I stayed up late, so I went out to find something to eat. It was so delicious! The two of us ate three bowls! I highly recommend the duck leg noodles!

author: Khay Yin Tang
review_text:
⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

I was pleasantly surprised to find that this restaurant is entirely staffed by women, including the chefs! The atmosphere was welcoming, and the food was absolutely delicious. Every dish I tried was full of flavor and beautifully presented. I highly recommend this place to anyone looking for a great dining experience!

author: Chow Stephen
review_text:
Open kitchen concept, surprisingly all female employees from front desk till kitchen.

We arrive is queue outside prepare chair for waiting, while waiting let you view menu and take order, mention to ours 20mins, after seating clean up the dishes are serve direct, manage well on timing.

Kem som taste normal spicy,
Egg omelette nice
Fried pork belly garlic nice
Broccoli with shrimp nice
Pepper ginger pork slices taste good
Petai Shrimp very nice.

NON-HALAL
Not plenty of parking lot
Environment clean and neat
Price cheap 6dishes with 7pax 705baht

Highly recommend

author: Notorious
review_text: First dinner here on my trip. The first thing you notice is the huge window into the kitchen, where it looks like an all-female team of chefs is at work. The food is tasty, well-seasoned, and flavorful. Communication is easy too—no problem with English here.

author: C J
review_text:
I loved their tomyam, spiciness at the very nice level. I ordered shrimp tomyam, it comes with 6 medicum sized shrimps and the portion is good for 2 people.

Waitresses are friendly and helpful by offering chairs while waiting to be seated inside.

Parking is not hard to find.

author: Supat Limsakul
review_text:
The food is delicious, flavorful, and the portions are generous. The ingredients are of high quality.
The service is fast and efficient.

author: Li Yuen
review_text: Tried this Thai restaurant and really enjoyed it! The fried seabass with chilli sauce was slightly spicy and tasty with a nice crunch, but the tom yum soup was definitely our favourite… so flavourful and comforting. Will be back again!

author: Elanggo Krishnan
review_text:
Shop is very clean.
Tomyam seafood taste great.
Sea fish not fresh but cooking flavor taste well.
Stir Fried Seafood with Curry Powder taste good too.
Basil Pork moderate taste.

author: yin jia goh
review_text: Nice food with reasonable price👌😋 but I think tomyum soup can be more spicy abit

author: Chong Lip
review_text:
Very nice Authentic Thai Food! Best in Hatyai!!!
Michelin standard! 😍😋👏🏻👏🏻👍🏻
In summary, best of the rest!😋👏🏻👏🏻👍🏻

author: Jeff Chua
review_text: Food is nice. Service is good. Got English menu available. Price reasonable

author: Stacey K
review_text: Another pleasant surprise. A restaurant we went after seeing long queue outside the restaurant for a few days. Good and cheap Thai dishes. Dishes portion more suitable for 1-2 pax

author: Aves Khiung
review_text: Good foods. Place is clean. Open kitchen with many staffs. Foods are served very quick after order, maybe due to at least 7 staffs in the kitchen.

author: Kuan Fung Chin
review_text: Friendly staffs, fast service, good food, reasonable price

author: EWE DE LUNN
review_text: Loved by the local, the food very nice, tomyum can choose the spiciness, fried vegetables good to taste, fried squid is a must!!

author: Lee Hoon Loh
review_text: One of the best local Thai Food restaurants ever tried compare to those other over high rated restaurants, this one very good 👍🏻

author: Wen Chien Cheang
review_text: We ordered these dishes for 4 adults. More than enough, love the big portion served. They had an open kitchen, the kitchen is clean, able to watch the chef cooking performance too. Noticed most of the chefs are women, the staff were friendly too. Most importantly, the dishes were cheap, value for money.

author: Sujie Won
review_text: Nice place to have some simple Thai Food😋. Tom yam is spicy 🌶️ the veggie is the best especially I love the Kailan 👍👍👍. Will visit again 😉

author: CS Lim
review_text: taste very nice with reasonable price. need to queue, but won't wait too long

author: Mauricio
review_text: Ordered a curry paste chicken ala carte, and frankly it was disappointing. The chicken were small fragments of bone with tiny slivers of meat. Taste-wise it was ok, nothing out of the ordinary. Poor value.

author: Peter Tan
review_text: Good place to eat. affordable price, clean and new. thai and Chinese style cook food

restaurant: Buffet Rimnam Mookata And Seafood Hatyai
author: EXOL & NCTzen
review_text: Too many options of what to eat from their fresh seafood, fishballs section, meats, ready to eat food, their desserts and more. Overall food here is very good and delicious. The seafood is fresh. U can either cook yourself or ask them to cook for you. There are some you  can make to order just have to let them know your table. Their drinks also have many options. Service is also very good. Just that if u are not local, u may need to go by ehailing as it’s quite far from the main city. Recommend to try. We all came out full and happy.

restaurant: Buffet Rimnam Mookata And Seafood Hatyai
author: Bordin Jindawattanawong
review_text: This is one of the best mid-to-high-range buffets in the city. I loved that many dishes were cooked-to-order rather than sitting under heat lamps, which kept everything tasting fresh and premium. We decided to go for the 498 Baht seafood package instead of the basic tier, and for the most part, it was excellent value. However, the reason I’m not giving it a full 5 stars is that I was really expecting to see fried mantis shrimp with garlic on the menu for this price point, but unfortunately, they didn't serve it.

restaurant: Buffet Rimnam Mookata And Seafood Hatyai
author: Teng Sook Yin
review_text: Wide range of food and varieties. Given 2 charcoal stoves. One for Mookata and for BBQ. Can choose to cook ourselves or ask them to cook, especially the larger items like fish and crabs. The seafood is fresh. The salt grilled fish was delicious. Just the environment was very hot due to heat from the stoves. But that is expected I guess. Not all areas can be installed with fans. Still enjoyed the meal.

restaurant: Buffet Rimnam Mookata And Seafood Hatyai
author: Ju Nguyen
review_text: The diversity of the food, the food freshness, the service, the outdoor atmosphere, everything is excellent if you have a big stomache.

restaurant: Buffet Rimnam Mookata And Seafood Hatyai
author: W T
review_text:
Visited what I’d call the best seafood mookata spot I’ve tried in Hat Yai, and it was an unforgettable experience. At around 500+ baht per person, the price is slightly higher than most local barbecue places, but I personally feel it’s worth every baht for the quality and variety offered. The seafood selection was outstanding — fresh river prawns, squid, clams, and fish, all prepared perfectly for grilling.

What makes this place unique is a special section where you can hand over your chosen raw ingredients for the staff to cook according to your preferred style, which adds a personal touch to the meal. I focused mainly on the seafood, which was flavorful and fresh, while my companion sampled the meat and felt it wasn’t quite on par with the seafood. Still, for anyone craving a satisfying seafood mookata experience in Hat Yai, this spot is definitely a must-try.

restaurant: Buffet Rimnam Mookata And Seafood Hatyai
author: Eskimo 0308
review_text:
25feb25.Anybody wanna join me tonight? I am solo traveler.
Finally manage to taste the food. Value for money. Many dishes didn't try because I solo dining. Next trip will come with friends. The staff polite and friendly. So sad as 8pm they stop service prawn cooked vermicelli.

restaurant: Buffet Rimnam Mookata And Seafood Hatyai
author: Jess Lim
review_text:
No time limit, you can eat from 4pm to 11pm

Extensive selection of seafood, dessert, vegetables and meat.

You get to choose the cooking style for the seafood you have chosen.

The waitress cleaned up the table and refilled the food on time.

Not air-conditioned but the place has good ventilation.

restaurant: Buffet Rimnam Mookata And Seafood Hatyai
author: Yuri Tan
review_text: Worse experience ever do not eat here if Yr here, here's recap on my part, my family was trying to enjoy the buffet yes we ordered the normal package we payed around 300baht, but when we eating the next table besides us ordered the package that includes premium seafood, they offered my family a crab, and and then the workers came by and warned me us once tht we can't eat the seafood, Ok look BUT is the table next to us offering to us, and then the second time the worker comes and they did not say anything about they will charge my family table extra 298 baht just because OF ONE CRAB that the other table offered, they also stated they will charge if they seen us taken the item BUT the sign they pointed at IS NOT FOR THE PRICING that they gonna charge if anyone taken the seafood

restaurant: Buffet Rimnam Mookata And Seafood Hatyai
author: yow suen tho
review_text:
Quite extensive seafood if early. If late, also still well stocked.
