review_text: Very nice ambiance. Great food and service. We got the set meal, pho, scallops, and coconut juice.

author: Viaan Dodhia
review_text: Queen was amazing and helped me with my first time hotpot which I had at this beautiful restaurant. The staff is super friendly and excellent ambience and service. Must come for great food and awesome view.

author: anais siba
review_text: The place is beautiful and quiet. A lots of space so you don’t feel to much pressure. Also the view on the river is lovely. The waitresses are professional and nice. The food was tasty and well proportioned 🫶🏼

author: Hien Duong
review_text: An excellent place to try authentic Vietnamese food in Hoi An. Everything was fresh, flavorful, and reasonably priced. The service was warm and welcoming.

author: Nguyen Thanh Tam
review_text:
This restaurant offers a beautiful and peaceful atmosphere, with seating options indoors, in the garden, and by the river.

The menu features a variety of Vietnamese dishes, not only from Hội An but also from across Vietnam. The flavors are thoughtfully adjusted to suit different guests, ensuring that the food isn’t overly sweet or greasy while still staying true to its authentic essence.

The staff are nice and caring for our needs

author: Ct Harwanie
review_text: I order a scallop. The scallops are a standout—each one delicately topped with a medley of herbs and peanut that add freshness and texture. A squeeze of lime brings everything to life, enhancing the natural sweetness of the seafood.

author: Jeffreyl Ella
review_text:
We ordered Coconut coffee and it did not disappiont us. The blend of coconut into coffee is so perfect, the coffee is strong and the creminess of coconut is the perfect combination. It has also crush coconut.

The place is quiet so you can have your relax moment and just watched the people walking outside.

Staffs are also welcoming and accomodating, there plenty of them so they can assist you right away.

This is a best place when you are with your friends after you ate lunch or dinner just to talk and have your relax moment.

Oveall, will definitely comeback here.

author: p p
review_text:
One of my favorite cafés in Hoi An. The drinks are reasonably priced, and you can relax and enjoy the river view while sipping your coffee.
The coffee tastes great and isn’t expensive.
The staff are friendly and provide excellent service.
Highly recommended!

author: samay vora
review_text:
Cong Caphe, just opposite the river, is a cozy and inviting spot.
The seating is comfortable, with a great view to enjoy while you relax.
Wi-Fi is strong, making it perfect for working or long chats.
You can easily sit here for four to five hours without any rush.
The ambience has a rustic charm with a unique vintage vibe.
Their signature salted coffee is a must-try – rich and flavorful.
Overall, a great place to unwind, work, or simply enjoy Hoi An’s calm.

author: Apple Ong
review_text: Cộng Cà Phê only accepts cash and does not take credit cards. This generally applies to most places in Hoi An. We loved the drinks here. They only serve beverages and do not offer desserts or food of any kind.

author: Bhavika Gondhalekar
review_text: I was looking for a place to have a nice coffee. I came across cong caphe as their reviews were nice so I decided to go there. I ordered vietnamese cold coffee, It was really very good. Worth it! Also the ambience was great!

author: Jayne Collins
review_text: Decided to go for one of their signature coffees, and opted for the coconut green rice ice coffee, it was like drinking rice pudding and totally delicious. The other drink we ordered was the iced coconut coffee, again delicious. Really nice peaceful part of Hoi An right on the riverside, so pleased the pilot on our flight recommended it to us. Excellent spot to escape the busy streets

author: Chutikarn Sukchote
review_text: Love everything about hoi an, especially this cafe. Good coffee, good vibe, good spot to take pic and talking chilling. The coconut coffee is a bit sweet for me but overall would be 9/10!

author: Jherson Jaya
review_text: Nicely located in front of the Hoi An River. Its nice to sit here and just observe the people. They have fast wifi too!

author: Franz Jeunesse
review_text: Cong Caphe in Hoi An is really a vibe! The atmosphere really lives up for Ancient Town type of chill. Minimal lighting inside the cafe. Less people compare to the other branch in Da Nang City. Most of the staff can speak english

author: June Thorfun
review_text:
Cong Caphe has a really cool vibe with its vintage military-style decor and cozy atmosphere. The mix of antique wooden furniture, Chinese cotton print cushions, and soft lighting makes it a great spot to take a break while exploring Hanoi. There’s a nice mix of seating, from lounge chairs to wooden tables, and the whole place has a nostalgic, slightly retro feel.

The drinks were just okay—not bad, but nothing too special. Still, the unique ambiance makes it worth a visit, especially if you like cafes with character.

author: Subhankar Dey
review_text:
Cộng Cà Phê is one of my favorite coffee chains in Vietnam. It beautifully preserves the authentic values of the country's history. The thoughtfully curated interiors always remind me of Kolkata’s vintage charm. The coffee is quite good and reasonably priced. The staff wear uniforms that evoke the spirit of a significant movement in Vietnam’s past, adding to the immersive atmosphere. If you sit by the window, you can enjoy a charming view of the river and watch the boats gently pass by.

The name "Cộng" is inspired by “Cộng sản,” meaning “communism,” reflecting the café's nostalgic tribute to Vietnam’s historical era.

author: Kiều Nguyễn Thị
review_text:
The space is quite nice and the drinks are excellent, especially the coconut coffee, which I really liked. However, the staff’s attitude was truly disappointing. They didn’t seem cheerful or friendly, and appeared irritated with customers. I noticed one staff member (K. Linh), whose attitude was particularly bad — definitely not suitable for the service industry. Good drinks won’t make customers come back if the service is poor.

On the bright side, the manager was friendly, calm, and had a good attitude.

author: Charles C
review_text: Clutch coconut coffee. I always dread when the drink is almost over. I find it very refreshing on a hot day. Just like their other locations, you can expect a good, consistent drink here. There is plenty of seating in this location.

author: sarah lloyd
review_text: Great branch of the Cong Caphe! Managed to sit in the lovely seats outside the cafe overlooking the river. The coconut coffee here is the best I’ve had while in Vietnam, very creamy and delicious! Only downside is that they didn’t have any of the food advertised available, however the coffee is great!

author: Panploy Kunket
review_text: Super hot!!! But understandable cuz we can’t control the weather tho😂 no air conditioner but fan. Coconut coffee is so gooooooooood👍🏻

author: Sumit Saudagar
review_text:
Rating: ★★★★★ (5/5)

Cong Cafe in Hoi An is a must-visit for coffee lovers! The cafe has a cozy, vintage atmosphere with a unique retro charm that makes it stand out. I tried their signature Vietnamese iced coffee, and it was rich, strong, and absolutely delicious. The ambiance is relaxed and welcoming, perfect for a casual hangout or enjoying a quiet moment. The staff was friendly and provided excellent service. The prices were very reasonable for the quality and experience. If you’re in Hoi An, don’t miss out on Cong Cafe for a true taste of Vietnamese coffee and a lovely environment!

author: Yi Wang
review_text: There are two levels where you can select your seating. I opted for a cinnamon chocolate beverage, which was incredibly creamy and bursting with a decadent taste. During the early hours of Monday, between 9-10am, the place is not very crowded. The ambiance is enhanced by the soothing sounds of old-time jazz music, making it a perfect setting to enjoy a meal and unwind.

author: Ashley Hung
review_text:
We had coconut iced coffee, which is like liquid coconut coffee ice cream, very delicious!  The cafe is located in the heart of old town Hoi An and right across from the Thu Bon River.
p.s. Cong Caphe tote bags also make great souvenir gifts for friends!

author: Hiep Nguyen
review_text:
Cong Caphe is the best. We had it in SaiGon and loved it. Glad they have one in Hoi An too!

Service is just efficient and friendly. I had knocked down my drink before even taking a sip. It was all over the floor. Within seconds 1 guy came and cleaned up the mess, another server got my another drink made in 1 min. No questions asked. That is amazing customer service 👏.

Great atmosphere and they got fans blowing from all sides. Feels nice and cool during the 30° C day. 130,000 Dong for our drinks is $7 CAD.

author: Renee Richter
review_text: Interesting coffee shop. The drinks are unusual, most are mixed with tea. We enjoyed it.

author: Ed Seet
review_text: Local meals with broken rice. The food and service is good. Go early or there'll be a long queue. Grilled chicken Thigh and Pork Chop were very nice. Tried the pumpkin flower with garlic... Not my kind of vegetable dish though... Broken rice, a must try.

author: ECA
review_text:
Good spot within a row of establishments. Good food and great service too!

Food was good, but I have no way to tell if this is better or worse than other Com Tam spots in Saigon.

I personally had the Bun Cha which tasted like the other Bun Cha I had eaten on this trip. Perhaps the consistency across all restaurants should tell me that that is how Bun Cha should taste.

Worth a visit if you’re in the area!

author: lynn koh
review_text: I din a lot as I was full. I ordered the grilled pork and fried spring roll. Overall the food was good! Especially the grilled pork. The service was above averaged, we was serve by a young guy, he recommended their must try food n beverages. He was very friendly.. Thumb up to him! Please keep it up.

author: Porter KHOR
review_text:
Food not great.  Vi Da Vietnamese eatery at Ben Thahn market was so much better.  Feels like typical chain restaurant using frozen meats cooked without any soul.

My pork chop and braised pork belly tasted like microwaved leftovers. Dry and hard at some parts. Don't get fooled by photos on menu.  The real dishes all turned out alot smaller.  Crab meat ball is one good example.

Pricey not great.  Walk out for better food .  I'll never be back here again.  Bill was 480k for two pax

author: Joyce DV
review_text: Food is bland. Staffs would ignore you. Prices does not include tax or service charge. We ordered bun cha but did not give us water for the rice paper until we asked for it. Will charge you for wet tissue. The only thing interesting in this restaurant is the interiors. Do yourself a favor and eat somewhere else. 😭

author: Trung Nguyen
review_text:
This isn’t a large place. It’s well decorated, very hip. The walls are made of brick so voices bounced quite a bit. Fortunately the patrons keeps the voice down, but unfortunately some the waiter would yell across the room breaking the silence.

The food average. Nothing stands out. Though the portion is generous amount of meat in comparison to others.

It appears to have 4 person in the front (waiters), I don’t know how many in the back. They are so so slow. My rice plate took forever and it wasn’t just off the grill, so don’t know why it took this long. Amazingly my Pepsi took longer than my rice plate. And the finally, my goi cuon came out last.

author: Jessica Le
review_text:
I had such an amazing experience dining here! From the moment I walked in, the staff were warm, welcoming, and attentive without being overbearing. The atmosphere was cozy yet modern, making it perfect for both a casual meal or a special occasion.
The food was absolutely outstanding — every dish was fresh, flavorful, and beautifully presented. You can really taste the quality of the ingredients and the care put into the cooking. My personal favorites were Cơm Tấm, but honestly, everything we tried was delicious.
Service was quick and efficient, and the team made sure we always had what we needed. Prices are very reasonable for the portion sizes and the quality you get.

author: xin
review_text:
The deco and ambiance were nice, but it was very noisy inside. The food was average (as ive had better broken rice roadside stalls) and the cleanliness wasn’t great, I even found hair in my food.

The staff also need more training, as the service was quite poor. Overall, not the best experience.

author: Joe Kwong
review_text: In Saigon Centre, B2 floor (Ho Chi Ming city) you will find this little Vietnamese restaurant. Looks like they’re serving different broken rice here, it’s authentic and tasty. Besides, we found other dishes are really nice too, the taste of their food is just right and details, with reasonable price as well. Recommend.

author: Zoe Kay
review_text:
I’ve been in Vietnam for a couple of days and I couldn’t find anywhere that had that fresh vietnamese food i was looking for, until I found Com Tam Moc!!

I had a Vermicelli Noodle Salad with Pork and it was so amazing, exactly what I needed.

The staff didn’t speak much english but they always made sure you were okay and used Google Translate when needed.

100% Recommend

author: YAGIZ “CollageUSA Drive”
review_text: waitress was rude, chicken wasn't cooked enough (its risky for health), only good thing about restaurant was atmosphere but I pay for eaiting not atmosphere so 1 star only

author: Kien Tran (Kin)
review_text:
ok this one kinda nice cơm tấm (broken rice) spot i’ve hit in saigon recently, maybe the best for tourist. it’s a bit pricey for cơm tấm and def feels a little catered to tourists, but honestly… i’d still go back.

the sườn nướng (grilled pork chop) hits hard—perfectly caramelized edges, juicy inside, the marinade’s that sweet-savory goodness done right. the cơm (rice) itself’s fluffy and lightly fragrant, not dry like at other places. big win: they give plenty of mỡ hành (scallion oil) and mắm chấm (fish sauce dip), balanced just right—not too sugary, not too pungent. love that.

skip the soup unless you’re really craving side quests.

author: Ly Chou
review_text: definitely recommend this place, if you want to try Vietnamese food, they have a variety of foods n their staff are so nice, some can even speak a little bit of Khmer. The atmosphere is so cozy, not crowded too, WOULD COME HERE AGAINN⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️

author: Casey Chong
review_text: Nice atmosphere, food you can get anywhere nothing special but the service level is for local Vietnamese. Plenty empty free table and yet asked us to squeeze with other 2 seater tables

author: Bree Reeves
review_text:
10/10
Exposed brick wall, beautiful high ceiling, warm wood. I might have to keep ordering so I can stay here longer 😍
The food. Delicious!
(Ut khon) my server was helpful - service overall was friendly and well run.

author: Andrew Wong
review_text: Ordered the grilled chicken and steamed vegetables platter with braised fish sauce. Enjoyed the meal, place was cosy with fast service, price was reasonable considering it’s a restaurant with AC.

author: Stan Mellstrom
review_text:
The reviews on here are chatting absolute rubbish. i had the BEST meat dishes from here and the atmosphere is super chill. clean facilities and the workers did their best considering the language barrier.

Remember people always try for yourself!

author: The Laughing Lion
review_text:
I thought this place was good, not spectacular or bad, but good.
The flavors of the grilled pork chop were as expected. My only complaint was of the spring rolls. The rice paper they used was kind of tough. I am accustomed to soft spring rolls, so I was a bit surprised.
The dining room was basic and clean. The tables and chairs were all made of wood. I went for lunch and it was not very busy, so the service was really quick. The staff was friendly.
The prices are very reasonable here considering this is in a tourist zone.
I would definitely come back here and have a meal again.

author: Cindy Woon Lee Loo
review_text: Food is better than expected.. ribs , pork and vegs are delicious... with broken roce of course...

author: Thanh-Mai Nguyen
review_text: We had a delicious meal here. Food was tasty, staff was friendly, and the restaurant vibes were cool. Highly recommended

author: Jhon Melky Chumacera
review_text:
I recently had one of the best coffee experiences in Ho Chi Minh City at Trung Nguyên Legend Café on Alexandre de Rhodes — and it’s easily my favorite among the many branches in the area. What makes this location special isn’t just the coffee, it’s the whole atmosphere that feels both cozy and timeless.

The moment you sit down, you’re greeted by a space that somehow blends old-world charm with relaxed sophistication. The interior is warm and inviting, with comfortable seating that makes it perfect for lingering over a cup, while the outdoor seating lets you soak up the vibrant street life of Ho Chi Minh City without feeling rushed. Many other branches are nice, but here the setting feels particularly magical — like a cherished local secret where coffee culture is celebrated.

The coffee itself is exceptional. Trung Nguyên’s deep roots in Vietnamese coffee culture shine through in every sip, offering a rich, aromatic profile that exemplifies why this brand has become iconic.

Service is attentive without being intrusive, and even when busy, the pace doesn’t suffer. It’s the kind of place where you can enjoy both the buzz of the city and a moment of peace with a beautifully brewed coffee.

Highly recommended for anyone who wants a genuine, memorable coffee experience in HCMC.

author: An Le
review_text: This location is massive and very clean—definitely more of an upscale vibe if you need a break from the heat. The drip coffee is very strong (just how I like it) and the pastries were fresh. Picked up some beans as gifts too. Great spot to just sit and chill for a bit

author: Ryan G
review_text:
The Trying Legend Caffe is one of those rare places where you don’t simply come for a cup of coffee—you come for the experience. Tucked away in a corner of Ho Chi Minh City, it feels almost unreal how quickly the atmosphere shifts the moment you step inside. Despite being in the heart of one of the busiest and most energetic cities in Asia, the café somehow creates a peaceful bubble that makes you forget the traffic, the pace, and the noise outside. It’s the perfect spot to slow down, breathe, and simply be present.

The colours of the space immediately set the tone. Warm earthy tones mixed with thoughtful accents give the café a calm, inviting charm. Every detail—from the lighting to the layout—feels intentionally chosen to help visitors unwind. But it’s the flavours that truly elevate the experience. Each drink is crafted with care, whether you go for a classic Vietnamese brew or one of their more unique signature creations. The balance, the aroma, and the richness are consistently impressive.

What truly sets The Trying Legend Caffe apart, though, is the level of experience they offer. The staff are kind and attentive, the ambiance is soothing, and every visit feels special. It’s beyond amazing—an oasis in a bustling city, and absolutely worth returning to.

author: Tia
review_text:
We visited this café because it was very eye-catching, and it definitely delivers on atmosphere. The space is elegant and pleasant, and the coffee was genuinely amazing.

The only downside for us was the presentation of the food. We ordered the sunny-side egg bánh mì and it arrived deconstructed, which we weren’t expecting. While the flavours were good, we weren’t provided with a knife to cut the bread and assemble it ourselves, which made the whole experience a bit messy and more complicated than it needed to be.

Overall, the café has a great vibe and excellent coffee, but a little more attention to food presentation and basic cutlery would really improve the experience.

author: cindy ngo
review_text:
If you are a coffee lover then you should try to see if you can take a strongest coffee here or not as it is a very special coffee represented to Vietnamese  coffee culture.

Price: acceptable

Location: located at the city center which is from the coffee shop you can walk around the park the heart of the city, as well as independence palace, Catholic Church, diamond plaza around 5’ walk.

Event for: family gathering, friends meeting even business meeting also fine as it is not so noise and I saw there was a private meeting area available as well.

In conclusion, it is a good place for tourism or even local relaxation.

author: And S
review_text: Went to this outlet of legend cafe not knowing it is a chain. You go for the experience, it’s a bit pricey but has a nice atmosphere. Service is a bit slow. Had the legend coffee which is a drip coffee in an espresso cup. With 189k VND it’s very expensive, but comes on a nice tray and is supposedly made of fermented coffee beans. Taste was exceptional.

author: Ibizian Ibizian
review_text:
This place is amazing. The service is definitely 5 ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐. They brought us a menu and some very delicious tea. Those cups were never empty. They made sure you had tea, and that's before you even order and after you've had your coffee and food and are just relaxing. The tea kept coming!

The coffee... What can be said about Vietnamese coffee that the world doesn't already know!

Presentation was great for first timers. They taught her how to process and then drink her coffee. And of course it was unlike any coffee at home!

Definitely a place to pop in, get some AC and chill!

World class!

author: Hoàng Quỳnh
review_text:
This Trung Nguyên spot near Notre-Dame Cathedral is a familiar name in the area. It’s been around for quite a while and offers a classic setting, especially convenient if you’re meeting someone in the city center.

One plus: They offer table service – you order at your seat and pay after, which is convenient and makes things smoother when you’re hosting guests.

But the downsides?
• Mosquitoes. Yes, even when you’re sitting in air-conditioned areas, you’re still getting bitten. No joke.
• Staffing is thin – sometimes it’s hard to get a waiter’s attention.
• And of course, Trung Nguyên prices are no joke – drinks can be pricier than Starbucks or most high-end coffee chains.

Overall: Great location and service concept, but between the high prices and the uninvited mosquito guests (yes, even indoors), it’s more of a once-in-a-while stop than a regular hangout.

author: Tita Pizza
review_text:
This coffee shop caught our attention due to its numerous branches, prompting us to give it a try. We opted for the Zen coffee, which appeared to be their specialty, but it fell short of expectations, especially considering the steep price of VND 189,000. Given its status as a specialty coffee shop, we anticipated a more engaging experience. However, the server simply lit the burner and left without any explanation, leaving us unsure of how to enjoy the unique presentation.

The coffee itself was quite potent and not to our liking. On a brighter note, the Salt Coffee was enjoyable and somewhat redeemed the visit.

Overall, we wouldn’t highly recommend this place, as there are better coffee shops available.

Tip: If you're considering purchasing their packed coffee, it's more affordable at grocery stores like Co.OP Mart.

------

Warning for tourists: while crossing a pedestrian, we were suddenly "guided" by a local street peddler - we didn't ask for directions nor tell him where we were going but he just said "4 blocks away". I initially just said thank you because I had a bad feeling he will ask for something in return "in exchange" for the help. However, he suddenly talked to my companion and asked where we were from as we were walking. Before I knew it, we were being asked to pay for fresh coconut juice (VDN 150,000 each). He was so quick to open 2 coconuts that we didn't have a choice but as he was opening the 3rd one, we said "no need, just 2" but he got mad and proceeded to open the 3rd one anyway. All in all, we paid VDN 450,000 for 3 coconuts. Talk about highway robbery. So disappointing.

Lesson learned: really do not talk to strangers.

author: Zarina Kurtnizirova
review_text: I found shelter in this cafe when it started to rain. I like the way they serve their food. The coffee was good. I also ordered beef stew, it was so comforting in such weather. Absolutely recommend this place.

author: Nurul Hisham
review_text: We had some Vietnamese coffee and their special iced milked tea. They were super good. And we bought some coffee beans, coffee powders and a few coffee drip press or coffee filters to bring home as souvenirs ❤️

author: XianYan Wu
review_text:
Coconut pandan coffee is good. Banana pancake crepe is tasty but too small portion. Coffee was pretty good, we tried #5 and #4. #5 is better and balanced. #4 is more coffee and sweeter.

Environment is beautiful and tastefully designed. Free tea given to all guests. Spent 260k Dong for 3 drinks, 1 dessert.

author: Botak
review_text:
The review address for this should be:

7 Nguyễn Văn Chiêm, Bến Nghé, Quận 1, Thành phố Hồ Chí Minh 700000, Vietnam

Not sure how I should go about amending it

Love this place as a great place to chill and have my Vietnamese coffee, plus you can buy coffee souvenirs for friends before  leaving HCM

Personally, I prefer this compared to Starbucks and Coffee Bean as u get to see more locals and their families there.

But try not to go on weekends since it is normally quite difficult to get a seat.

Staff are polite and price slightly lower than the American chains.

A legend not to be missed.

author: Ekk Chawa
review_text:
This cafe is beautiful. The front is like mountain and forest and inside is like a library where the books replaced by coffee cans and bags. There's also an  elegant piano place in the center.
I ordered Napolian coffee and my colleague had dried Pho. The coffee was super strong and gave me energized for the rest of the day and Pho was delicious.
Good place for chilling or have a nice meal.

author: Eileen Reichenbächer
review_text: If you would like to try some delicious Vietnamese coffee specialities, then I can highly recommend this café. The menu offers selected drinks and dishes, although the price is a bit too high. The staff are friendly and happy to advise you on your choice. Enjoy your visit in a relaxed atmosphere with delicious coffee. ☕🍰

author: DONLAWAT PANRAT
review_text: The food and coffee are excellent, the service is friendly, and the location is nice. It's also pleasantly cool inside thanks to the air conditioning.

author: Rapin P
review_text:
Mosquito lots on second floor ,
Food quality and coffee price . Really not for me :-( sorry

author: Bas Barath
review_text:
I didn't enjoy their legendary signature coffee. Firstly, it took 30 mins to get my drink due to mixup, and then the drip coffee takes more than 15 mins to actually drip into the cup through the filter. I didn't get my cake either, and they couldn't be bothered to at least tell me they were out of it.

I guess, if you have plenty of time in your hand, this may be a nice place to hang out. It's hard to be a patron here with limited time.

author: Adrian Nc
review_text:
Drink is good.
Price is more than high - almost 10 times compare to the cheapest one - but reasonable as its trademark and location.
But the most inconvenient thing is hardly to find a power socket (next to your seat) to charge the phone or laptop

author: Khoa Do
review_text: Good location to begin your day with a delicious coffee and breakfast. Nice decoration with separate spaces, inside for ppl who wanna have business talk or a reunion of old friend; Outside with park view for whom wanna take a breath of fresh air in the morning. Bike parking is always available. Recommend coming at Morning.

author: LML
review_text: After learning that Michelin awarded this restaurant a Bib Gourmand, I had to try it—and it did not disappoint. The phở gà was excellent, with a rich, flavorful broth. The restaurant was packed with locals, which added to the authenticity of the experience. I ordered a small portion after reading reviews that mentioned the generous sizing, and it was indeed more than sufficient.

author: Holland Mills
review_text:
We did not have this location on our radar prior to a recommendation from our friends at Cà Phê X, but it's firmly on there now!

Down a side alley and nearby the aforementioned Coffee experience, this unassuming eatery has been an institution of Hanoi style Chicken Phở for over 25 years!

We really enjoyed the flavorful no-frills broth, the herbs and fixings served alongside, and the opportunity to see the entire operation at work during our meal.

The pricing is very affordable, and the meal is filling. It wasn't until after our visit that I noticed the Bib Gourmand awards on their wall, almost delivery tucked away from the main event.

We'll be looking forward to our return here next time we are in HCMC!

author: naengbu
review_text:
Classic Pho Ga! 🍜🇻🇳
I had to stop by the famous michelin bib restaurant serving chicken pho in HCMC. You know it’s gonna be good when the place is filled with locals.

I ordered their signature dish: Pho Ga (Chicken Pho). As an Indonesian, this is a dish  resembles a dish called soto ayam back home. A simple warm dish, just noodles, chicken and aromatics. Perfect for a rainy day. The chicken was cooked to perfection, tender and fulfilling. The broth was extremely rich, too rich for my liking, which put me off from finishing the broth. I added condiments and leaves they provided to really elevate the experience.

Despite its reputation, the prices were still reasonable, and the portion sizes were generous, a great value meal. We left barely able to walk.

The service was top notch. Even though we were the only tourists, they served us well and were VERY attentive. None of them spoke English, but they still tried their best to accommodate us 🫶🏻🙌🏻. We often feel out of place in Vietnam, but they made us feel welcomed. They took cleanliness seriously too.

It’s a little far from district 1, but I recommend making the trip if you’re ever nearby. See you again👏🏻

author: Cindy Woon Lee Loo
review_text: Had the beef Pho, spring rolls etc. The broth is good and you can add your own vegs into your bowl. Overall its yummy and per serving is quite big for an Asian serving.. need to take Grab to get there..

author: Lionel Lim
review_text: First visit to this famous Chicken Pho and I was not disappointed at all. The bowl of chicken Pho might look plain but once you start, you will realize why this place received so much accolades. The broth is light and flavorful, very tasty and goes very well with the noodle and chicken parts.

author: Wahlin Lee
review_text: We liked the pho here very much! The broth is very flavorful. It has a very subtle hint of chicken, but after squeezing in some calamansi, the flavor was elevated, becoming beautifully clear and sweet.  We will come back for sure.

author: Jane Le
review_text:
Chicken Noodle – Michelin Guide

Every time I visit Vietnam, I make sure to stop by this chicken noodle shop. The chicken here isn’t as soft as what you might find in Singapore, as they use local farm chicken, giving it a firmer texture — especially in the salad and noodle dishes.

I also recommend trying the fresh sugar cane juice. On my latest visit, I tried the guava juice with sour plum too — it was freshly made and really refreshing!

author: YUUKI SUGIYAMA
review_text:
My visit to Phở Miến Gà Kỳ Đồng was a long-awaited treat. Despite it being on my list since day one, the fun of travelling with friends meant I only managed to get here on my last day in Ho Chi Minh City. Yet, the anticipation was well worth it.

As a Michelin recommended eatery, I naturally had to try their signature dish: the chicken pho. The soup base was what truly sets it apart. It was incredibly rich and hearty, yet surprisingly clean and sweet on the palate, a testament to hours of careful simmering. Each spoonful felt nourishing and deeply satisfying. The chicken was cooked to perfection so tender and succulent it practically melted in my mouth.

To elevate the experience, I added some fresh basil leaves, which brightened the broth with a lovely, fragrant lift. A splash of fish sauce introduced a new layer of complexity, adding a savory depth that transformed the flavour profile entirely.

Despite its prestigious recommendation, the prices here are astonishingly reasonable. I was genuinely surprised when a bowl of their famous chicken pho and a drink came to just 85,000 VND. It's an incredible value for such a high-quality meal.

This place is an absolute must-visit for anyone in Saigon. It’s an unforgettable culinary experience that proves great food doesn't have to be expensive. I’ll definitely be making a return visit on my next trip to the city.

author: The MY World
review_text: It's Phở and Miến restaurant, which was selected as Bib Gurment by Michelin. I remember that it was located on the very small street, but after few years, the steet was a bit developped and cleaner than before. Anyway there are many tables, so you don't need to worry for the table. You can have. We had Pho and Mien, then Pho 's soup came with fried garlic and the Mien's soup came with Onion, so it tastes a bit different but the base was same. Then the soup was awsome. I think this Pho Ga and Mien Ga was the best bowl in my life, also in Vietnam. Last time, I could not recognize because of lack of my experience, but after I had so many popular noodles all over the Vietnam, I can recognize. I want to come back again.

author: Rachael Wong
review_text: Delicious bowl of chicken pho, broth is very rich and flavorful. Tender chicken, fresh herbs, just right. A bit far out, but worth the trip. Service is friendly, place stays clean.

author: Abbie Diem
review_text: The food was good, they don’t use too much sugar so the broth is not too sweet. The portions are small though. The chicken meat is firm.

author: Celine T
review_text: My personal favourite in HCMC. I’ve been here 3 times now - the first back in 2023 and it was life changing. The chicken pho is just as good 2 years later. It is chicken soup for the soul manifested in real life. I’ll continue dreaming of the day I can have this pho again.

author: Irene
review_text: This is a must-visit place for me every time in HCM. I went back so many times during my trip there. The soup and the chicken tasted perfectly. Can’t wait to come back!!

author: Irene F
review_text: Love the soup noodles and the salad. You can choose your noodles with the same soup base. Our group chose the glass noodles, thin egg noodles and pho noodles. We loved the chicken salad with lotus root and banana blossoms.

author: RYSA
review_text: the pho broth was unimpressive, saw many good reviews but was disappointed with it. tasted like MSG, doesnt taste good at all compared to other phos i have tried in hcmc. maybe try once is good but will not come back again for the pho

author: Richard
review_text: Perfect for a rainy day. Got the chicken pho and vermicelli. Both were good. Chicken salad was also very good. I do wish the broth had a slightly stronger chicken flavour.

author: 招财喵
review_text:
The Michelin recommend chicken pho.
The taste is just ok for me, not a must to visit, their homemade chili sauce is nice!

author: Yee Win Maw
review_text:
Pho but only chicken.
Taste 9/10
A little but far from city center
If you want to try pho and don’t eat beef, this is one of the options.

author: Che P
review_text: The staff are very attentive, Pho Mien Ga has amazing flavors, the clear broth is very savory, and the chicken is very juicy 10/10 experience. They don't speak English, but they are very welcoming to foreigners. Also, they accept cash only. Cash is king in Vietnam.

author: Joey Lu
review_text:
Had a super shiok meal at Phở Miến gà Kỳ Đồng.

We ordered the pho with chicken breast, egg noodles, and a chicken salad to share.

The broth was light but full of flavour, and the chicken was fresh and tender. The herbs and bean sprouts added a nice crunch, really made the bowl more satisfying.

The chicken salad was refreshing, got a good mix of herbs and onions. The iced black coffee was strong, just nice to finish off the meal. Place has a nice local feel, very straightforward, busy but no fuss.

Just take note it’s cash only, so better bring enough.

Will definitely come back for another bowl when I’m around in Vietnam.

author: Katharina Brandau
review_text: Awesome coffee place in HCMC, if you are into speciality coffee. Staff take their coffee seriously. They give great recommendations and show their different brewing methods and utensils. The place itself is on the 3rd floor, industrial design and nice decor. Loved it so much that we took a 20min walk just to come back here for a nice V60. Got beans, too.

author: Ann Ng
review_text:
☕ The Workshop has a cool industrial-style interior with spacious seating and plenty of natural light. The bar is lined with coffee equipment, creating a professional vibe — a great spot for coffee lovers.

This is my third visit, and the food and drinks are still up to standard:
• Pour-over coffee: aromatic, smooth, and beautifully presented.
• Omelette with toast & salad: fluffy, tasty, and just the right portion.
• Croissant: crisp, buttery, and perfect with jam and butter.

The only downside is that the staff don’t seem very welcoming — a warmer smile and friendliness would make the experience even better.

Overall, still a great place to enjoy coffee, breakfast, or brunch. 🌟

author: Janine Chang
review_text:
great cafe on the 3rd or 4th floor (can't remember which exactly). they seat you and present the menu for you to select from. the prices are a little higher, though they take their coffee seriously so it's definitely for those with a high appreciation of coffee. everything we had there was delicious! my sister-in-law isn't a coffee person but loves tiramisu and loved theirs.

they have a restroom on the same floor, outside of the cafe.

author: Polevy Ezekiel
review_text: One of the most recommended specialty coffee shop in Ho Chi Minh called @theworkshopcoffee, established since 2014 and located in the bustling Bến Nghé area. Located on the second floor of an old 1912 building, the classic vintage ambience feels very strong because many architectural elements are very well maintained. High ceilings with many window openings from various directions create good natural lighting, causing a warm, comfy and welcoming space. Various coffee menus are served here and the ones I recommend most are classic coffee and manual brew with various of the best coffee beans from various origins.

author: Leonard Lim
review_text:
Workshop Coffee in Ho Chi Minh City is one of those places that stands out for its cool, industrial-chic vibe. It’s always lively and full of energy, popular with Chinese tourists and expats alike. Their coffee is excellent, and although the food menu is quite limited, everything I’ve tried has been tasty.

The only downsides for me are that the entrance is a bit hidden—you have to go up a flight of stairs to find it—and it can get really crowded and noisy during busy hours. Also, I personally find the chairs quite uncomfortable, which makes it hard to sit for long.

author: Giovanni
review_text: Definitely the place where to have nice food and where to work at a laptop. They're built for that, there are plugs everywhere and the wifi is strong. The staff will not bother you, but it's good habit to order something every hour at least, and tip the staff appropriately. The food is good, big, and vote expensive. Good quality place.

author: Chuin Ling Ung (CL)
review_text: It's a quite hidden kind of cafe if you don't really notice the signboard. It's kinda cute though. The variety of coffee served here are really special and are so good. Tried their nutty cremina and salted iced coffee, and I can say the salted iced coffee is a must try! Panna cotta gives off a very balanced taste and it's really good.

author: Dallas D
review_text:
A beautiful loft-style space with true European vibes — spacious, high ceilings, great light. As someone who loves lofts, I felt right at home.

Built a couple of documents here and genuinely enjoyed the atmosphere.

Excellent espresso, and big thanks to the team for creating such a well-designed environment for focus and creativity.🫶

author: Chlotus
review_text: This is a lovely little cafe where we can take a break from our walking tour! It's tucked away in a building, giving it a cozy feel. The coffee here is delicious and has a nice strong flavor. It's a popular spot for people working or studying, but it's a bit too quiet, almost like a library.

author: S Marie
review_text: Nice café with a good view and fine for a quick stop, but the drinks were disappointing. I asked for Vietnamese coffee for my latte, and they didn’t have it, which was surprising. The baristas also weren’t flexible with adjusting the sweetness or replacing the sweet milk with fresh milk. The service was okay, but the overall experience was average at best.

author: piglene
review_text: came here to complete some work. i think the chair is a bit painful to sit in for a long time. it was a bit difficult to find the cafe since it is through a small corridor and up the stairs but it really feels like a hidden gem. a friendly local street vendor had to help us and point us to the cafe to find it. plenty of electrical plugs available and the staff with provide you a multi plug if you need it! it is just the right temperature but gets really really noisy when it starts raining 😭 i enjoyed the food! the service is perfect for introverts. not much smiles and attention but they will help you immediately if you asked for it!

author: Gildwen LE FERREC
review_text: A known place for the coffee drinkers. Great busy-coffee « bar » where one can meet friends, do some coworking in dedicated spots, enjoy the taste of coffee and learn new grain type and tastes. They have great food as well and really offer a precise coffee making. Highly recommend!

author: Lionel Sim
review_text:
I visited The Working Coffee recently and left dissatisfied with the service experience.

Service was slow from ordering to drink delivery, despite the café not being overly busy. The staff member handling my order, Vy, appeared overwhelmed and uncoordinated with the rest of the team. There was visible confusion behind the counter, with staff moving in overlapping paths and frequently bumping into one another.

There was also no clear or systematic ordering process. Customers were unsure where to queue or who was responsible for taking orders. Tasks seemed to shift between staff members without clear ownership, which contributed to delays and disrupted workflow.

The café has potential, but the lack of structured operations and clear staff coordination significantly impacted the experience. A defined ordering system, clearer role assignment, and better internal communication would improve service efficiency and customer flow.

author: Ming Dao
review_text:
This has been one of my go-to coffee shops since the early days of specialty coffee in Vietnam. After 9 years, it still feels the same.

Great coffee. Delicious food. A space that strikes a quiet balance, not too loud, not too quiet. The large windows open to a beautiful city view

More than just a coffee, it’s a place that still carries the spirit of old Saigon

author: Miley Cyrus
review_text: It wasn’t very easy for me to find the entrance, I at first thought I’m at a wrong place, but look at the entrance in my pictures if u got confused like me😹 I paid 175.000vnd for this omelette 🍳 prices are about 45-100 for the drinks and 130-200 for the food.  it’s a bit expensive for me but it was delicious and cooked very fast. I recommend this place to visit 👍🏻 u can bring ur computer and work here but today around 6pm it was a bit crowdy. It’s not quiet but also not noisy.

author: Hazel Ta
review_text:
Very mid if not tasteless coffee (latte) and non-coffee (oolong cold brew) drinks 😰

The ambience was amazing which is why the ratings got 3* and why we even came back. Metal chairs with limited support for your back so it will get uncomfy for long sitting and somehow the tables are super low??? (I’m not even that tall…)

Staffs were unwelcoming and borderline rude to Vietnamese customers, when we came in it was crowded and they told us to sit at the large shared table despite having a vacant window-side table. They put the reserve sign on it, but when we about to leave a female staff came and said we could sit there (?). I paid 200k for 2 mid drinks and 1 cookie yet they were annoyed when we ask for our free parking tickets 🥀??? Much better support and hospitality for other Non-Viet customers

Guess this is one of those places that only welcomes foreigners like the ones in Thao Dien =)))

author: Tommy Tang
review_text: This place is wildly famous! Though the street-level sign is so small you'd easily miss it. Entering the first floor feels like walking into a condemned building. You'll need to navigate narrow, steep stairs up to the third floor. The coffee and cakes? Decent but forgettable. The staff are lovely though - which almost makes up for the completely uninspired food.

author: Asli Leone
review_text: Great spot for breakfast and getting some laptop work done with a solid cappuccino. It’s spacious, with power outlets, reliable Wi-Fi, and decaf coffee available. It tends to get busy after 10 a.m., so if you need a quieter atmosphere, it’s best to go early when they open at 8.

author: Billy Fyfe
review_text: Great place…tough to find, you have to go up three floors but that’s normal in Vietnam, I love it. Definitely recommended. Good coffee and the Benedict was perfect.

author: David Nguyen
review_text: Great place for digital nomads looking to do some work. Great views near the windows and lots of coffee options from pour over to specialty flavors.

author: Dani Calvo
review_text: this food was incredible. favorite dish was definitely the bep cuon combo 2. the pork and shrimp pancake rolled into the spring roll provided was an incredible array of flavor. we also ordered the tom su sot bo toi an kem banh bao chien, which was good as well, a little less savory than expected, but delicious. finally we ordered the Ba Chi Gion Da Mam Tac. the sauce it came with was incredible and the crispy edges of the pork were delicious. definitely recommend to stop by for a bite.

author: Bowen Chau
review_text:
Bếp Cuốn Sài Gòn is a delightful culinary gem nestled near the city center of Ho Chi Minh City, making it easily accessible via Grab. This Michelin-recommended restaurant offers a refreshing twist on traditional Vietnamese cuisine, setting it apart from the usual pho-focused menus.

Upon entering, you’re greeted by a cozy yet stylish decor that reflects a modern take on Vietnamese aesthetics. The intimate size of the restaurant fosters a warm atmosphere, perfect for enjoying a meal with friends or a loved one.

The staff at Bếp Cuốn are incredibly friendly and eager to guide you through their unique offerings. They are passionate about the menu and are happy to recommend dishes that showcase a fusion of flavors, blending classic ingredients with innovative techniques. Each dish is a testament to the chef’s creativity, bursting with fresh ingredients and vibrant tastes.

The food is nothing short of delicious, with each bite inviting you to savor the harmonious blend of textures and flavors. Overall, Bếp Cuốn Sài Gòn is a must-visit for anyone looking to experience a modern twist on Vietnamese cuisine in a welcoming setting. Don’t miss out on this unforgettable dining experience!

author: YUUKI SUGIYAMA
review_text:
My group of five stumbled upon this delightful Vietnamese restaurant in Ho Chi Minh City, and what a find it was. The decor immediately catches your eye, with its rich, traditional Vietnamese touches that make you feel truly immersed in the local culture.

Given that we didn't have any specific recommendations from social media, we decided to be adventurous and simply order whatever caught our eye from the picture menu. To our absolute delight, every single dish was a winner not a single bad choice in the lot!

A standout was the grilled pork belly. It was perfectly cooked, with a wonderfully crisp exterior that gave way to tender, juicy meat. Paired with a spicy dipping sauce, it was incredibly moreish and surprisingly light. We also thoroughly enjoyed the grilled pork with rice noodles. I’ve had this dish before in Laos, and the flavours here were just as authentic and delicious a testament to the shared culinary heritage of the region.

What makes this place even better is the price. For a group of five, we were able to enjoy a fantastic, satisfying meal without breaking the bank. A brilliant spot for anyone looking for a genuine and affordable taste of Vietnam. Highly recommended!

author: Sherilyn Tran
review_text: We stumbled upon the restaurant by chance, and it turned out to be the best decision. The food was sensational—we ordered two bánh xèo, one spring roll, and one rice soup, and everything was served without a long wait. The staff were very attentive, and the wonderful employee, Hera, showed us how to eat bánh xèo the right way! Truly the best bánh xèo I’ve ever had! Thank you for the great experience—we will definitely be back

author: R Kim
review_text: We were looking for ban xeo and saw the high ratings for Bep. Food was very good expect the chicken skewers which were dry as if they had been precooked and kept in a warming tray. Really no excuse for that. Skewers grill frairly quickly.  Other than that, the staff were very friendly and the setting was warm and inviting. Love that the wet naps were free!

author: Irene Lee
review_text: We ordered the signature platter, fried mushrooms and fried prawns. All the dishes didn't disappoint but lack the wow factor. Maybe we came with high expectations as it is a Michelin restaurant. We thought the fried mushrooms would go well with Vietnamese sauce instead of the Japanese sesame sauce. Strange to have jap sauce in a Vietnamese restaurant.

author: Lowella Tay
review_text:
We ordered the bep cuon platter as well as the bun cha and everything was amazing. Cant choose which was my favourite since all was equally good. Definitely a must try when in Ho Chi Minh!

Service from Nhu Y was also great! She showed us how to eat the banh xeo and it was very delicious.

author: Sarah Lee
review_text:
Mixed appetizer, fried chicken wings and crispy pork were good and were the only items we think were made from scratch.

The rest were just alright - stir fry beef with instant noodles, pan fried pork with frozen fries, pineapple fried rice with frozen pea and carrot mix…No draft beer

Staff were very hospitable and restaurant was well air conditioned.

Good for quick lunch stop

author: Nava Neetha
review_text:
Food here was delicious!! The flavours were fresh and bold (and loved that we could ask for free flow vegetables that were crunchy and for
more sauces). I was here 3 times in the 1 week I was in HCMC!! The service is excellent too. Would definitely recommend🤗

author: Sibu Pitse
review_text:
We had our 1st meal in Vietnam at this Michelin selected restaurant. Kai masterfully showed us how to eat the rice cakes with garden salad. Everything was fresh and absolutely delicious.
Thank you Kai for the great service.

author: Travel_Love
review_text: Food was good, but I ate better rice pancakes. I didn't like that when I asked if I can sit upstairs, the waitress told me that no because of the "rest time" (whatever it means). Then new customers came in and they allowed them to sit upstairs without any problem.

author: Jani Valkonen (JayValkyr)
review_text:
This Michelin-selected restaurant comes with high expectations. We had lunch here and it was good. Nothing exceptional, especially compared to the dinner we had last night almost by chance.

Still recommended and absolutely worth a
visit.

author: Annie. Travel and Food
review_text:
The restaurant has a charming ambiance with tasteful décor, creating a pleasant dining atmosphere. The staff were attentive and genuinely friendly, which made the experience welcoming.

As for the food, the flavors were decent, though not outstanding. Unfortunately, the seafood did not meet expectations — the squid lacked freshness and was slightly mushy, while the shrimp had a noticeable odor. The bánh xèo was flavorful but overly greasy, which made it feel heavy. The dipping sauce had a rather unusual taste that may not suit everyone’s palate.

I would still consider returning to try other dishes, hoping for a more balanced flavor and fresher ingredients next time.

author: alex kelly
review_text: Food was absolutely delicious and the staff were amazing. Specifically Hera! She went above and beyond helped show us how to eat roll the  Banh Xeo! Would highly recommend if you're traveling to Ho Chi Minh.

author: Netta Szekely
review_text: Come here if you just landed in Vietnam and want the tourist friendly version of street food. And I mean it in every good way as we came back here couple of times. Everything we ate here was delicious. Try their pre set combo plates, morning glory and pork belly. Yum.

author: Us The Creators
review_text:
platter gives you everything you need to try when you’re here! a nice restaurant to dine and try out (almost all) the vietnamese food you gotta try.

priced slightly higher than others but the food quality is good!

author: Cha Gomez
review_text: Kai (Staff) kindly granted my request for a smaller portion of Bep Cuon! The original platter for was supposed to be for sharing but I dined solo here, they modified the order and gave me 2pcs of each. Just right for me finish 🇻🇳❤️ and I did finish everything! They very much deserve the michelin recognition.

author: Osaka Nov17
review_text: Traditional Vietnamese food, the dining experience is good. Only ordered 2 dishes and a shrimp congee. Congee is sweet. The dipping sauce for steamed broccoli is tasty. Overall environment is nice.

author: Koong 8142
review_text: Fresh ingredients with a wide variety of menus. I love how the waiter took time to teach us the right way to enjoy Vietnamese Bua Sae—made the experience even more special!

author: GT Nguyen
review_text: My family of 9 came in for brunch and we had a great experience. Grandpa has a wheelchair, so we sat on the first floor. Most of Vietnam isn’t accessible, but this restaurant was as most accessible as it could be. The food was sooo good. We almost over ordered but our server informed us it might be too much food and she was right. I’m so glad they didn’t try to oversell us. The service was awesome they really care about their customers. Hera was our server and she was AMAZING! You should definitely give this place a try when you visit HCM

author: Joshua Fields
review_text: An excellent operation with a chill vibe and a creative menu, taking amazing meals up a notch in unique ways. The Tartare Crostini is well formed and very flavorful, the salad’s cream and seasonings took some mixing up to get used to but that was good. Brown butter Crab with bread was great, and my two favorite starters the Grilled Octopus and the Seafood Rice. The octopus had perfect char and a sweet delicious taste paired great with the egg. The Seafood Rice was a great blend of fish stocked rice and cold fish as a topping. Then the Pork Collar, I loved this it’s a perfect preparation. Great portion with a beautiful seasoned top layer and a wonderful fatty center. We didn’t care much for the side, which for a dish this pricey you’d like solid side as a base but this gets a pass. Lastly to finish off the Panna Cotta was straight up great, safest dessert option.

author: Justin Godbout
review_text:
Bravo. I’ve determined that this would officially be my last meal. Everything was perfect. The restaurant itself is super cosy. The service was excellent, relaxed. The food was interesting and flavourful. We tried a number of fun wines that paired well our food.

My only complaint is how hard it was to get a reservation 😆

author: Nomadicus
review_text:
Four Horsemen feels like stumbling into a very well kept secret that somehow never tries to impress you… and still does.

I decided to try getting in without a reservation and luckily they thoughtfully keep bar and window seats available for walk-ins. The best approach is to line up right when the kitchen opens, or wait until the initial 5pm dinner rush tapers off and secure a seat at the bar.

The dining room is quietly romantic but a bit snug nonetheless creating a relaxed, understated atmosphere. Service is genuinely warm and technically precise without a hint of theatrics, striking an ideal balance of professionalism and ease.

The menu consists of tapas-style plates that are intentionally restrained. With minimal ingredients and thoughtful execution, each dish allows the quality of the product to shine rather than relying on excess or embellishment. The result is food that feels confident, focused, and deeply satisfying.

Four Horsemen is refined without feeling formal, and thoughtful without being precious, making it a place worth the effort, even on short notice.

author: Meredith Oliver
review_text:
I enjoyed Four Horsemen, but it didn't blow my mind for the price. If I went again, I'd stick to the small plates so I could try more things. The chicken was good, but not great and it was huge. Their menu changes on a regular basis, so you can't be sure what you're going to get. Nothing I had was bad. Wagyu crostini and harimasa (not pictured) were my favorites.

I arrived at 10:45am, and waited for them to open at 11. A line formed quickly, and it's a slow process for them to seat everyone in their tiny space. If you can't get a reservation, show up as early as you can.

author: brandi brady
review_text:
I really enjoyed every bite and the service was great! the server had lots of great suggestions on food & pairings. we were a party of 4, walk in. for me, it makes it extra special when you stand in line for a seat & secure it in the first seatings. the hiramasa & green tomatoes are my fav, the glazed beetroot & mushroom toast were great. the mackerel was good, it didn’t knock my socks off the way everything else did.
looking forward to when I can get over there for lunch!

author: Mohamed Izlanshah
review_text: exceptional. dare i say one of the best meals ive had in my life. from start to finish every bite and every sip is so well thought out, so stunning and so so delicious. complicated flavours served in a non pretentious setting, laid back sunday lunch in the best restaurant in brooklyn. life changing stuff.

author: Patrick K
review_text: Michelin star wine bar? Yes pls! But people come here for the food. Impossible to snag a resy but worth waiting for a walk in spot at lunch or before dinner service. Vibe cozy and cute. Food was amazing! Small menu but basically every dish was a hit. Also the wine selection was well curated.  Verdict: recommend and will return!!

author: Lili McFarlane
review_text: Not a single miss. Everything was standout, flavors are thought provoking. For 2 people we shared the mushroom toast, fennel salad, bread, hiramasa, pork collar, and halibut. Toffee pudding for dessert. Portions are smaller but with this order we left full. Service was excellent especially for recommending wine.

author: Sally Nguyen
review_text: This restaurant is overrated, and I honestly don’t understand how it has held a Michelin star for several years. It’s definitely not worth the price. The portions are tiny, the flavors were either far too salty or overly acidic. Despite spending over $200 for just five dishes for 3 people , none of us left feeling satisfied. On top of that, getting a reservation here is unnecessarily difficult. For the same price, we had a much better experience at Theodora, which doesn’t even have a Michelin star but served food that was both delicious and filling. Save your time and money—skip this place and go somewhere else.

author: Delphica Sibyl
review_text:
The Four Horsemen - finally  😊
My husband and I have been devoted LCD Soundsystem fans for years, so the fact that James Murphy co-founded this place has always made it feel like a small dream waiting to happen. We’d been postponing it for weeks, as life has a way of reshuffling plans, but this time my husband said, 'This is your birthday and that’s it. We’re going.' I agreed ;)
The restaurant itself is small, understated, and effortlessly elegant. The interior has that kind of simple chic that feels authentic: warm wood, soft light, no pretense. We didn’t have a reservation but decided to take a chance, and after waiting about thirty minutes, we got a table right after 5:20 pm
The menu is tiny, almost minimalist, but every dish feels deeply considered. We weren’t too hungry, so we ordered a few small plates and a bottle of wine, saving room for dessert and hoping for a candle later.
And the food… oh, the food. I’m not sure words can do it justice. Every bite was a perfect balance of acid, sweetness, and texture. I’m from wine and vinegar country, so I truly appreciate the taste of acidity and here, I finally found a place in New York that speaks to my palate. Their flavors don’t fade the moment you swallow; they linger, evolve, and make you think.
I couldn’t help but notice almost everyone around us was ordering their famous warm bread, it looked absolutely divine. But since I bake my own bread at home and had already had a fresh loaf that morning, we decided to skip it this time. Still, it clearly seemed to be the must of the evening, and I’ll definitely try it on our next visit.
The wine list is impressive. We chose a French white that was absolutely balanced, bright, and beautifully alive (and no headache after!). And the desserts… I’m still dreaming about the passionfruit cake, so light, tangy, and joyful. I was especially happy that nobody from the staff sang 'Happy Birthday.' ❤️
As for the staff, 'perfect' doesn’t even begin to describe their service. They have that rare ability to make you feel both taken care of and completely at ease.
The atmosphere, the music, the people, the vibe: 10 out of 10, or maybe 100 out of 100.

To Be Continued
:))

author: Marvin Fuentes
review_text: The four horsemen has to be one of the best dining experiences I’ve been to this year. Everything was exquisite from the presentation to the music. But all the credit has to go to our Bartender Will; his knowledge of wine and bitters and amaro is renowned with some of the best in the game. Sit at the bar and thank me later

author: AC Slater
review_text:
Can't wait to return. Everything was incredible, especially the oeuf mayonnaise- which is forever engrained in my memory as one of my favorite bites anywhere.

Queued up 30 minutes before opening and the line filled up FAST

author: Noe Amighini
review_text:
The experience was bad from the start, when they seated us at a bar facing the street next to the entrance door, which opened every two minutes and froze us. There were four empty seats at the other bar, and we asked to change, but they said no, that they were busy, even though no one was sitting there. On the other hand, the food is scarce and not very tasty for what they charge, especially for a restaurant that is supposedly recommended by Michelin. We ordered rice with seafood, and it was almost impossible to find. For starters, we had mayonnaise eggs that were cold!!! They didn't warn us, they were tiny, not incredible and the price was extremely high. In conclusion, if you want to eat ordinary food, meager portions, nothing particularly sophisticated in terms of flavor, and pay a fortune... this is the place!
Oh, the bread was very good!

author: Jack Bekos
review_text: One of my favorite meals in NYC this year. Every dish was a dream. We ordered the oeuf, green tomatoes, fennel salad, tartare, mushroom toast and rainbow trout. Latter two were our favorites. The passion fruit tart dessert was magical. The best part? The wildly inventive wine list that paired perfectly with every bite. Service was great and homey, intimate setting was wonderful. Expensive but worth it for a special occasion.

author: Maria
review_text:
Tiny spot known for his extensive wine list and ever-changing (short) menu.
We started with the bread and clams which pairs perfectly together - thanks to the suggestion of our waitress.
Next we had the green tomatoes dish which was our favorite by far as it was packed with so much flavor and seasoned to perfection.
We finished with the Golden Rice topped with Uni which was delicious as well.
Highly recommend this Michelin star spot for a date night!
*Resys are a must unless you get there right at 5pm and get a bar or window seat

author: Khoi Pham
review_text: Interestingly enough, my personal favorites were the smaller dishes rather than the larger ones. Notably, the oeuf mayonnaise and the warm house bread (the butter especially) were great. Otherwise, everything else was fine although nothing too particularly memorable. The staff is very attentive and helpful. The vibes are lively but also serene, which I like.

author: Audreanna
review_text: Some dishes were fantastic while others weren’t. The summer squash was drowning in Beurre Blanc and rather gross. The fried crab was soggy. The pork shoulder was delicious. The service was overall good but slow. Their wine selection is one of my favorite things about the experiences. Overall I found the four horsemen to be mid for this type of restaurant and expectation.

author: Yulia Shekeladze
review_text: everything was delicious (although deep fried mackerel wasn’t out favourite, it had a very fishy taste) and this place absolutely deserves the hype. also we went without reservation, i got in line at 4:45 (saturday night) to put my name down for a group of 3 and we were seated at 7:30, so it is definitely possible.

author: Jennifer Lee
review_text:
Finally getting around to writing this, but The Four Horsemen really lived up to the hype. The place is super cozy and welcoming.

Our server was awesome and gave us great wine recs that perfectly complemented the food. Everything we ate was seriously delicious—you can tell they put a lot of thought into every dish.

author: Julie Geng
review_text:
This was my third visit to The Four Horsemen since June 2024, and sadly, it was a sharp departure from the consistently excellent experiences I’ve had in the past.

The quality of the food has noticeably declined. They no longer serve the signature seared yellowfin tuna. The skewer was aggressively spicy, overwhelming rather than enhancing the flavor. The Gen clam dish came across as bland. The swordfish was dry and overcooked. Even the egg appetizer that people rave about felt uninspired.

Equally disappointing was the service behind the bar. The bartenders were visibly drinking while serving us, and one even spat into the sink right in front of us while we were eating. That kind of disregard for basic professionalism and hygiene.

It’s disheartening to see such a reputable place slip so far in both culinary quality and hospitality. I hope this was an off night, but given the steep drop in standards, I’m hesitant to return anytime

author: Komal Rathi
review_text:
Such a disappointment. Glad I went on a Tuesday morning at 9 AM when there were maybe a handful people inside and all the tables were available.

Salmon Foccacia was cold and hard. Had to literally chew the hell out of it. Earl grey morning bun was cold as well. Brown butter cornbread - again cold, dry and way too sweet. Only thing decent was the black forest croissant which was honestly just ok but better than the rest.

People who say that the smoked salmon focaccia is out of this world or the brown butter cornbread is the best thing to touch their mouth are probably living in a bubble. To say this is one of the best bakery in a city like NYC full of amazing bakeries is an abomination.

I honestly don't understand if you open at 7:30 AM and I am there at 9 AM how is everything so cold l, dry and hard? $60 down the drain. Well, at least I didn't stand in line for two hours.

author: Nam Nguyen
review_text:
On weekends, this establishment experiences a queue extending from the interior to the exterior, with an estimated wait time of 30 minutes for entry. The line typically progresses at a swift pace. Outdoor seating is available, and a Citi Bike station is conveniently located directly in front of the premises.

They offer a selection of delectable sandwiches and baked goods, all prepared fresh in-house. The staff is knowledgeable and readily available to address any inquiries. The croissant was particularly enjoyable. We highly recommend sampling the cornbread; it is, in my experience, an exceptionally delightful rendition of the item. Pricing is competitive with current market rates within the industry.

author: Joon Lim
review_text:
Oh my goodness.. Best focaccias I've ever tried.
All their pastries, especially the focaccia, were so soft and chewy on the inside and crunchy on the outside,
I had quite a few of them..

Smoked Salmon with cream cheese, dill, and picked onion.. damn well balanced.
Shakshuka Focaccia was so delicant it was unbelievable, and with an actual full-on egg inside.
Everythign Space with Scallion Cream Cheese was also amazing. The scallions were fresh and it gave a very fun texture and interesting taste that I loved.
Scallion Seasame Twist was another great one. My sister's favorite.
Lastly the Early Grey Bun. I'm not a big fan of earl grey but still picked it up.
I don't regret the choice!

Beautifully balanced taste on all their selections.

author: Minh Nguyen
review_text:
It's not bad but a bit overhyped. The foccacia and sesame twist are delicious but the rest of the pastries are just average:
- Croissant: no flavour whatsoever, the butter is completely missing
- Corn cake: rich but a bit too sweet. The inside is a bit gluey.
- Morning bun: can taste the early grey but also sweet, texture a bit dry
- Cinnamon rolls: also sweet and dry

Overall recommended to try if you are in the area but not worth travel the length of NY for...

author: Debisree Ray
review_text:
I’d heard great things about this Brooklyn bakery, so I finally stopped by on a Saturday around 1 p.m. As soon as I arrived, I saw a long line outside — and it continued inside as well. The shop itself is very small, with no indoor seating and just a few sidewalk tables, which fill up quickly. So my first tip: go early if you want the full selection and a shorter wait. The line does move fairly quickly, though, thanks to their fast service — and the crowd alone tells you how popular the place is.

Even though it was already late in the day and many items had sold out, I still managed to get a ham sandwich. It was fairly large  in size. I ate it in two portions ( however, I was not super hungry, tbh) and made with high-quality ham, a flavorful spread, and a sesame-crusted toasted baguette. The bread was a bit firm, but it seemed intentional. It wasn’t served hot, but it was fresh and made with high quality ingredients.

I also grabbed a slice of their brown corn butter cake, which was incredible — unlike anything I’ve had before. It reminded me of cornbread but with the richness and texture of a butter cake. A really delicious fusion.

To go with it, I ordered an iced mocha, and it was excellent. I’m usually picky about mochas, but this one had great balance: high-quality espresso and chocolate, thick texture, and just the right sweetness (leaning on the less-sweet side, which I loved).

Overall, this bakery is absolutely worth the visit — especially if you enjoy unique baked goods and great coffee. Just be prepared for a line, and try to arrive early for the best selection. I’m already planning to return and try more of their menu.

author: Rylan Gordon
review_text:
The pastries here are fantastic. Expect a line on a Saturday morning, but it moves quickly. We got the corn pecorino focaccia and were completely blown away — such a unique combination that totally works. I’m still thinking about it. We also got the brown butter cornbread, which was excellent, and topped it off with the cheddar pretzel bear claw. If you’re into pretzels, that one will be perfect for you.

They have so many pastries that you’ll want to come back a few times to try more. The service was very friendly, and everything looked amazing. Highly recommend stopping by if you’re looking for a great pastry spot in Brooklyn.

author: Ainishah Hemraj
review_text: pretty long line but i genuinely think the brown butter cornbread is worth it! the corn bread is balanced so well the crispy edges and soft inside and the brown butter adds the perfect flavour. the morning bun is also really good! i really liked the turkey focaccia but wish i had gotten one of the other focaccia sandwiches instead as they looked better

author: malhar kulkarni
review_text:
The hype about is true and 100% deserved!
Delicious fresh Sandos, Croissants and other bakery items. No matter what time you get here, you’ll find yourself in a queue (moves quickly). Some of the limited items drop at 7:30 am and get sold out quickly, some at 10:30 am. We tried Spicy Tofu, crispy cauliflower focaccia and they both were phenomenal. Pistachio Croissant is one of the best in NYC (competes with L’apartmente 4f) and is a must try. We’ll be back here to try our luck with the limited items!
Seating is outside only and very limited!

author: Ticha Ungboriboonpisal
review_text:
Radio Bakery is my no. 1 bakery in nyc. every time i go, i have to wait in line (~10-30 mins depending on which day and time).  what keeps me going back is their unique sandwiches and pastry 🥐 they always have rotating seasonal pastry and scrumptious collabs.

what i have tried—
✨apple brown butter croissant ($7): crispy croissant with sweet apple 🍎 it is not overly sweet; just enough to fuel my day.
✨smoked salmon focaccia ($15): a perfect breakfast or brunch. it is packed with cream cheese, dill, onion, and smoked salmon.
✨earl grey morning bun ($6): my all time fav. it is fragrant with early grey, cinnamon, in a chewy bun. i’d always go back for this.

i was actually going for corn custard tart but it was sold out within minutes 😭 people do not play when it comes to viral and seasonal bakery.

author: Daniela V
review_text:
Interior/outside terrace: the interior is very functional, very few inside seating options. But it’s not like a comfy café. They do have a small outside seating area, which is nice, nothing special, but if you get a table there, you can enjoy your croissants in the sun.

Food quality/price: good selection of savoury & sweet food, very delicious. I got an earl grey bun & a pistachio croissant. Both very delicious, like out of another world. Loved them. I found their food to be quite expensive.
Suggestion: why not making tiny versions of the different treats (to a smaller price as well of course), so solo-visitors can try more delicious treats?

Service: friendly, functional, nothing outstanding though.

author: Kongphop Attakowitwitaya
review_text:
Radio Bakery is such a charming spot! The bread and pastries are absolutely delicious, fresh, and full of flavor. The bakery itself is adorable, with a cozy and inviting atmosphere that makes you want to linger.

The neighborhood adds to the vibe too — it feels trendy and lively, making the whole experience even more enjoyable. Definitely a must-visit if you’re in the area and love good baked goods.

author: JC SORIANO
review_text: I don’t know man. Maybe because my wife makes some slammin focaccia, considering the line, I thought maybe the food here would be outstanding but, I found myself gnawing or needing to tear the sandwich from my mouth after biting down hard on the bread. I did see someone bite down and use their fingers to help them tear it away. My jaw muscles shouldn’t get tried from having to chew so hard to be honest 😅 Maybe they’re baking at too high of a heat who knows. The chocolate croissant however was “very good” not sure I would 15 minutes again to get a sandwich or pastries here.

author: J Howell
review_text: Everything this place touches is next level. The everything with cream cheese is unreal—so soft it literally melts in your mouth. You can taste the care and quality in every bite. Shout out to Billy for the great service—friendly, welcoming, and on point. Radio City Bakery is a must-stop.

author: Mia Huynh
review_text:
I've heard so much about this spot but never got the chance to go until recently. We went on a Monday morning around 11am, and there wasn't much of a wait but it was still packed inside nonetheless. They have a window bar for you to enjoy your pastries at, otherwise, all seating is outside.

We got their croissant, earl grey morning bun, apple brie croissant, and their roast beef sandwich. Everything was delicious. The favorite of the day was definitely the apple brie croissant—which I did not expect to like as much as I did. I loved how fragrant the tea flavor was in the earl grey morning bun, and loved how crispy it was. The croissant was also an all-around standard great croissant, and the roast beef sandwich was a heart lunch bite. Even though the pastries weren't warmed up, I thought they were so good and I would love to come back to try others!

author: Andrew Berto
review_text: One of the best bakeries in nyc!! I stopped by around noon on a Saturday and had to wait in line for maybe 20 min. The focaccia sandwich I had was incredible and def hit the spot. Now I gotta get up early and head near opening in the morning to catch the other pasties and seasonal treats they sell and sell out of. The peach iced tea was also very good

author: Ken F
review_text: I'll be honest, the food was alright. It seems like a low bar, but at least it's consistent and that's great. The service was good and it seemed like all of their customers were having a good time. They also know how to make an actual macchiato and not just call a caramel latte a macchiato. The cashier also made sure that we were aware of the macchiato size which would be very helpful for new customers.

author: HAIRmonstar
review_text:
"Finally made it to Radio Bakery in Greenpoint. As someone who runs a bakery myself, I was blown away by their operation. The open kitchen isn't just for show; it creates a lively, immersive atmosphere that draws customers in. You can literally feel the heat of the ovens and the passion of the bakers.

The balance of flavors and the texture were spot on. It was a great benchmarking experience for my next step. Highly recommended for anyone looking for inspiration in NY!"

author: sabrina
review_text: Decided to brave the line as it was my birthday and I’ve been longing to try the pastries here! Line moved swiftly and we got the everything focaccia with scallion cream cheese, cinnamon roll, earl grey morning bun, twice baked pistachio croissant, and heirloom tomato croissant; you can tell this stuff is crafted with so much expertise and creativity. I’m still dreaming of those flaky layers 🥐 We met the icon herself Kelly Mencin and she was so sweet and dropped off a fresh croissant 🥹 heaven!!
